descriptionByLocale.it:
Descrizione Posizione del dottorato: Modellazione di attrito in sospensioni colloidali 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Alla cattedra di Solid Mechanics (SMEC) dell'Istituto per i materiali da costruzione dell'ETH di Zurigo, ci proponiamo di capire come i materiali deformano, degradano, rompono e infine falliscono. La nostra ricerca è guidata dalla curiosità sui meccanismi fisici che sottomettono al fallimento e dall'ambizione di tradurre questa comprensione in materiali e strutture più affidabili e resilienti. Combinando la modellazione numerica, gli esperimenti di laboratorio e le analisi teoriche, cerchiamo di collegare i processi microscopici con il comportamento macroscopico dei sistemi ingegneristici e naturali e di sviluppare strumenti predittivi per il fallimento meccanico. Il nostro team è altamente interdisciplinare e internazionale, che riunisce ricercatori con sfondi in scienza dei materiali, meccanica e fisica applicata. Lavoriamo attraverso una vasta gamma di argomenti, tra cui la meccanica dei sistemi di particelle (colloidale e granulare), materiali progettati e topologicamente interlocked, la meccanica della fragilità nel collagene, la meccanica dei terremoti, la frattura dei materiali morbidi e la modellazione del fallimento nei processi multifisici come la degradazione del cemento a corrosione. Ciò che unisce questi sforzi è una curiosità condivisa sul perché i materiali complessi falliscono e l'impegno a sviluppare nuovi concetti, esperimenti e modelli che avanzano la nostra comprensione della meccanica fallita. Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato motivato e innovativo con uno sfondo in meccanica computazionale per lavorare su un progetto focalizzato sulla meccanica dei sistemi colloidali. Il candidato PhD condurrà la ricerca in un progetto collaborativo con i partner del Dipartimento dei Materiali ETH per scoprire i ruoli di attrito scorrevole e rotolante, e la loro combinazione, nelle proprietà reologiche delle sospensioni colloidali. Descrizione del lavoro
• Condurrete un'indagine computazionale e teorica sull'influenza dell'attrito interparticolare sulla reologia delle sospensioni concentrate
• Il lavoro si concentrerà sull'applicazione di modelli basati sulla fisica che collegano il comportamento attraverso le scale, dalla geometria delle singole particelle colloidali alla risposta macroscopica della sospensione
• Le tue responsabilità includono l'implementazione di simulazioni dinamici molecolari grossolane e l'esecuzione di verifiche e validazioni rigorose utilizzando set di dati forniti dai nostri collaboratori
• Il candidato lavorerà in stretta collaborazione con i ricercatori sperimentali all'interno del progetto, fornendo spunti di modellazione e aiutando a interpretare osservazioni sperimentali
• La posizione offre un ambiente stimolante per la crescita scientifica e la collaborazione Profilo
• Ha un grado MSc in meccanica, fisica, (civile, meccanico, aerospaziale, o bio-) ingegneria, scienza materiale, o una disciplina relativa
• Hai uno sfondo in scienze computazionali con un focus sulla meccanica solida, fisica applicata, o un campo correlato
• Hai esperienza nell'attuazione del codice scientifico, nel convalidarlo e nella verifica dei dati sperimentali
• Hai esperienza di programmazione precedente in Python e hai usato il controllo della versione
• Siete curiosi, automotivati e divertitevi a collaborare strettamente con gli sperimentatori
• Sei fluente in inglese (orale e scritto).

descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD position: Modeling friction in colloidal suspensions 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure. Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics. We are seeking a motivated, innovative PhD student with a background in computational mechanics to work on a project focused on the mechanics of colloidal systems. The PhD candidate will conduct research in a collaborative project with partners from the ETH Department of Materials to uncover the roles of sliding and rolling friction, and their combination, in the rheological properties of colloidal suspensions. Job description
• You will conduct a computational and theoretical investigation of the influence of inter-particle friction on the rheology of concentrated suspensions
• The work will focus on applying physics-based models that connect behavior across scales, from the geometry of single colloidal particles to the macroscopic response of the suspension
• Your responsibilities include implementing coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations and performing rigorous verification and validation using datasets provided by our collaborators
• The candidate will work in close collaboration with experimental researchers within the project, providing modeling insights and helping to interpret experimental observations
• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration Profile
• You hold an MSc degree in mechanics, physics, (civil, mechanical, aerospace, or bio-) engineering, material science, or a related discipline
• You have a background in computational sciences with a focus on solid mechanics, applied physics, or a related field
• You have experience implementing scientific code, validating it, and verifying it against experimental data
• You have prior programming experience in Python and have used version control
• You are curious, self-motivated, and enjoy collaborating closely with experimentalists
• You are fluent in English (oral and written).
• You enjoy working in a team, possess the necessary social skills and communication abilities, and contribute proactively to a positive group atmosphere Workplace Workplace We offer
• You will join a dynamic, international, and supportive research group that values curiosity, rigor, and collaboration.
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society.
• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university .
• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractiv
descriptionByLocale.de:
Beschreibung PhD-Position: Modellierreibung in kolloidalen Suspensionen 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken An der Professur für Solid Mechanics (SMEC) im Institut für Baustoffe der ETH Zürich wollen wir verstehen, wie Materialien sich verformen, degradieren, brechen und schließlich scheitern. Unsere Forschung wird von der Neugier über die physikalischen Mechanismen, die Misserfolg und den Ehrgeiz, dieses Verständnis in zuverlässigere und widerstandsfähigere Materialien und Strukturen zu übersetzen, angetrieben. Durch die Kombination von numerischer Modellierung, Laborexperimenten und theoretischen Analysen versuchen wir, mikroskopische Prozesse mit dem makroskopischen Verhalten sowohl technischer als auch natürlicher Systeme zu verknüpfen und prädiktive Werkzeuge für mechanischen Ausfall zu entwickeln. Unser Team ist sehr interdisziplinär und international und verbindet Forscher mit Hintergründen in der Materialwissenschaft, Mechanik und angewandter Physik. Wir arbeiten über eine breite Palette von Themen, einschließlich der Mechanik von Partikelsystemen (kolloidal und körnig), Architekten und topologisch verriegelten Materialien, die Mechanik der Fragilität in Kollagen, die Mechanik von Erdbeben, Bruch von weichen Materialien und Modellierungsfehler in multiphysischen Prozessen wie korrosionsgetriebenen Abbau von Beton. Was diese Bemühungen vereint, ist eine gemeinsame Neugier darüber, warum komplexe Materialien scheitern und ein Engagement für die Entwicklung neuer Konzepte, Experimente und Modelle, die unser Verständnis von Ausfallmechanik voranbringen. Wir suchen einen motivierten, innovativen Doktoranden mit einem Hintergrund in Rechenmechanik, um an einem Projekt zu arbeiten, das sich auf die Mechanik der kolloidalen Systeme konzentriert. Der Doktorand wird in einem kollaborativen Projekt mit Partnern der ETH-Abteilung für Materialien forschen, um die Rollen von Gleit- und Rollreibung und ihre Kombination in den rheologischen Eigenschaften von kolloidalen Suspensionen aufzudecken. Jobbeschreibung
• Sie werden eine rechnerische und theoretische Untersuchung des Einflusses der interteilchenförmigen Reibung auf die Rheologie konzentrierter Suspensionen durchführen
• Die Arbeit konzentriert sich auf die Anwendung von physikalischen Modellen, die das Verhalten über Skalen verbinden, von der Geometrie einzelner kolloidaler Partikel bis zur makroskopischen Reaktion der Suspension

Descrizione Position du doctorat: Modélisation du frottement dans les suspensions colloïdales 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Au Professeur de Mécanique Solide (SMEC) à l'Institut des matériaux de construction à l'ETH Zurich, nous voulons comprendre comment les matériaux déforment, dégradent, brisent et finalement échouent. Nos recherches sont motivées par la curiosité au sujet des mécanismes physiques qui sous-tendent l'échec et par l'ambition de traduire cette compréhension en matériaux et structures plus fiables et plus résistants. En combinant la modélisation numérique, les expériences de laboratoire et les analyses théoriques, nous cherchons à lier les processus microscopiques au comportement macroscopique des systèmes d'ingénierie et des systèmes naturels et à développer des outils prédictifs pour la défaillance mécanique. Notre équipe est hautement interdisciplinaire et internationale, réunissant des chercheurs ayant des connaissances en sciences des matériaux, en mécanique et en physique appliquée. Nous travaillons sur un large éventail de sujets, y compris la mécanique des systèmes de particules (colloïdaux et granulaires), les matériaux architecturés et topologiques entrelacés, la mécanique de la fragilité du collagène, la mécanique des tremblements de terre, la fracture des matériaux mous et l'échec de la modélisation dans des processus multiphysiques tels que la dégradation du béton par la corrosion. Ce qui unit ces efforts est une curiosité commune sur la raison pour laquelle les matériaux complexes échouent et un engagement à développer de nouveaux concepts, des expériences et des modèles qui font progresser notre compréhension de la mécanique de défaillance. Nous recherchons un doctorant motivé et innovateur ayant une formation en mécanique informatique pour travailler sur un projet axé sur la mécanique des systèmes colloïdaux. Le candidat au doctorat effectuera des recherches dans le cadre d'un projet de collaboration avec des partenaires du département des matériaux de l'ETH afin de découvrir les rôles du frottement glissant et du roulement, et leur combinaison, dans les propriétés rhéologiques des suspensions colloïdales. Descrizione Posizione del dottorato in studi numerici e sperimentali di sistemi granulari non sferica e deformabile 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo ETH Zurich è una delle università leader a livello mondiale ed è rinomata per la sua eccellenza nell'istruzione, nella ricerca fondamentale all'avanguardia e negli sforzi per mettere in pratica nuove conoscenze e innovazioni. Il Laboratorio di Scienza e Ingegneria Energetica (D-MAVT) sta lavorando attivamente allo sviluppo di strumenti numerici e sperimentali per sondare sistemi granulari mono e multifase (particolati). Sfondo del progetto I sistemi granulari sono onnipresenti in natura (ad esempio valanghe rocciose o dune) e di fondamentale importanza per l'industria. Tuttavia, nonostante il loro uso diffuso e il loro verificarsi, molti fenomeni importanti, come la segregazione, le instabilità della superficie o il jamming, cioè la transizione tra uno stato fluido- a uno stato solido, sono scarsamente compresi. Questo progetto esplora specificamente l'effetto della deformabilità delle particelle e della non-sfericità sulle dinamiche e reologia dei sistemi granulari. Le particelle flessibili si deformano sotto stress, mentre la deformazione a sua volta colpisce le forze di contatto e la trasmissione dello stress dando origine a fenomeni reologici complessi come il jamming transitorio o l'ordine orientativo indotto dallo stress. Anche se deformabili, i sistemi di particelle asferiche dovrebbero essere ricchi di fenomeni fisici, sono stati in gran parte evitati a causa di difficoltà nel fare misurazioni sperimentali in tali sistemi e nella loro descrizione numerica. Questa posizione PhD fa parte di un progetto congiunto che combina le competenze di due gruppi di ricerca ( Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering , Prof. Müller e l'Institute for Biomedical Imaging Magnetic Resonance Technology , Prof. Prüssmann) e gli studenti di dottorato assunti dai due gruppi coinvolti dovrebbero collaborare quotidianamente. Descrizione del lavoro L'obiettivo dello studente di dottorato assunto dal Laboratorio di Scienze e Ingegneria dell'Energia è quello di
• Avanzare strumenti numerici per modellare sistemi granulari non sferica e deformabile
• Stabilire tecniche sperimentali basate sulle telecamere come la foto-elasticimetria per determinare le forze di contatto e i campi di stress in tali sistemi
• Sviluppare e utilizzare modelli basati su machine-learning per correlare deformazione delle particelle e forze di contatto nei sistemi 3D Profilo

descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD position in numerical and experimental studies of non-spherical and deformable granular systems 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken ETH Zurich is one of the worldwide leading universities and is renowned for its excellence in education, cutting-edge fundamental research and efforts to put new knowledge and innovations directly into practice. The Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (D-MAVT) is working actively on developing numerical and experimental tools to probe single- and multiphase granular (particulate) systems. Project background Granular systems are ubiquitous in nature (e.g. rock avalanches or dunes) and of fundamental importance to industry. However, despite their widespread use and occurrence, many important phenomena, such as segregation, surface instabilities or jamming, i.e. the transition between a fluid- to solid-like state, are poorly understood. This project explores specifically the effect of particle deformability and non-sphericity on the dynamics and rheology of granular systems. Flexible particles deform under stress, while the deformation in turn affects the contact forces and stress transmission giving rise to complex rheological phenomena such as transient jamming or stress-induced orientational ordering. Although deformable, aspherical particle systems are expected to be rich in physical phenomena, they have been largely avoided owing to difficulties in making experimental measurements in such systems and in their numerical description. This PhD position is part of a joint project that combines the expertise of two research groups ( Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering , Prof. Müller and the Institute for Biomedical Imaging Magnetic Resonance Technology , Prof. Prüssmann) and the PhD students hired by the two groups involved are expected to collaborate on a daily basis. Job description The objective of the PhD student hired by the Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering is to
• Advance numerical tools to model non-spherical and deformable granular systems
• Establish camera-based experimental techniques such as photo-elasticimetry to determine contact forces and stress fields in such systems
• Develop and use machine-learning based models to correlate particle deformation and contact forces in 3D systems Profile
• Applicants for this PhD position are expected to have a very good MSc degree in Mechanical Engineering, Physics or related disciplines
• Previous experience in numerical modelling or imaging techniques is desirable
• We are looking for highly motivated, committed, and creative individuals, able to work in a team and with excellent communication skills in English, both oral and written

Das Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (D-MAVT) arbeitet aktiv an der Entwicklung von numerischen und experimentellen Werkzeugen, um ein- und mehrphasige körnige (partikuläre) Systeme zu Sonden. Projekt Hintergrund Granularsysteme sind in der Natur allgegenwärtig (z.B. Stein Lawinen oder Dünen) und von grundlegender Bedeutung für die Industrie. Descrizione Position du doctorat dans les études numériques et expérimentales de systèmes granulaires non sphériques et déformables 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken L'ETH Zurich est l'une des plus grandes universités du monde et est réputée pour son excellence en éducation, ses recherches fondamentales de pointe et ses efforts pour mettre en pratique directement les nouvelles connaissances et innovations. Le Laboratoire des sciences de l'énergie et de l'ingénierie (D-MAVT) travaille activement au développement d'outils numériques et expérimentaux pour sonder les systèmes granulaires monophasés et multiphasés (particules). Contexte du projet Les systèmes granulaires sont omniprésents dans la nature (par exemple les avalanches rocheuses ou les dunes) et ont une importance fondamentale pour l'industrie. Cependant, malgré leur utilisation et leur présence généralisées, de nombreux phénomènes importants, tels que la ségrégation, les instabilités de surface ou le brouillage, c'est-à-dire la transition entre un état de type fluide et un état solide, sont mal compris. Ce projet explore spécifiquement l'effet de la déformabilité des particules et de la non-sphéricité sur la dynamique et la rhéologie des systèmes granulaires. Les particules flexibles se déforment sous contrainte, tandis que la déformation à son tour affecte les forces de contact et la transmission de la contrainte donnant lieu à des phénomènes rhéologiques complexes tels que le brouillage transitoire ou l'ordre d'orientation induit par le stress. Bien que déformables, les systèmes de particules asphériques devraient être riches en phénomènes physiques, ils ont été largement évités en raison des difficultés à effectuer des mesures expérimentales dans ces systèmes et dans leur description numérique. Postdoctoral Researcher in Robot Learning 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Mobile Robotics Lab at ETH Zürich pushes the limits of robot intelligence: how can we design robot policies with a better understanding of the world humans live in? We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher in Robot Learning who is interested in questions such as:
• How can we fuse representations of the world with modern learning-based methods to allow for larger scale / longer horizon?
• How can we use Foundation Models, VLMs, VLAs, and robot learning for complex and long-horizon tasks that involve manipulation, locomotion, and navigation in potentially unstructured and large-scale environments? We investigate these questions on a number of real-world robots such as the Unitree G1 humanoid, Stretch 3, and drones. The Mobile Robotics Lab has various running research projects in the fields of
• Robot Learning
• Spatial AI
• Robot Perception
• Mobile Manipulation
• Navigation and Exploration For details about the individual running projects, please refer to our homepage . Job description
• Lead and shape an independent research agenda in mobile robotics, pioneering the use of modern learning-based methods such as but not limited to Foundation Models, VLMs, and VLA architectures for embodied intelligence
• Supervise and enable high-impact research on the lab’s humanoid platform (Unitree G1), pushing the boundaries of sim-to-real transfer and semantic reasoning
• Secure external funding (with strong institutional support) and build collaborations within the ETH ecosystem
• Co-supervise PhD and Master’s students, fostering a culture of technical excellence and ambitious experimentation
• Participate in teaching activities, including the development of new teaching materials in robotics, perception, and autonomous systems Profile
• PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field with impactful publications in top-tier venues (CORL, ICRA, RSS, NeurIPS, CVPR, etc.)

Postdoctoral Fellow in Volcanology and Magmatic Processes 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Institute of Geochemistry and Petrology at ETH Zurich is a world-leading center for research into the fundamental processes that shape our planet. We are excited to announce an opening for a Postdoctoral Fellow to work within the Volcanology and Magmatic Petrology group, led by Prof. Olivier Bachmann. Project background We are seeking a highly motivated and independent researcher to advance our understanding of magmatic and volcanic systems. Job description
• Develop and lead an independent research program in magmatic petrology, volcanology, and/or geochronology.
• Publish results in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals.
• Present findings at international conferences.
• Contribute to the teaching of BSc and MSc level courses in petrology and volcanology.
• Actively participate in the intellectual life of the institute and research group. Profile
• A recent PhD in Earth Sciences, with a focus on igneous petrology, volcanology, or geochemistry.
• A demonstrable ability to conduct and publish high-quality research.
• Strong analytical skills, particularly with in-situ techniques (e.g., EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, SIMS).
• Experience in field work, geochronology (e.g., U-Pb, Ar-Ar) and/or numerical modelling of igneous processes.
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. German speaking would be an added value. Workplace Workplace We offer This is a research-focused position with a teaching component, designed to help launch the career of an exceptional early-career scientist. You will be encouraged to develop and pursue your own research ideas, leveraging the extensive analytical infrastructure at ETH Zurich, which includes state-of-the-art microanalytical facilities (EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, TIMS), geochronology laboratories, and computing clusters. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. Descrizione Posizione dottorale nella cattedra di storia e filosofia delle scienze matematiche 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La cattedra di storia e filosofia delle scienze matematiche, guidata dal Prof. Roy Wagner, è un luogo per riflettere su tutti gli aspetti della conoscenza matematica dal punto di vista delle scienze umane. Il nostro team studia diverse culture matematiche storiche e contemporanee da una moltitudine di approcci metodologici. Sfondo del progetto Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato di condurre ricerche sullo sviluppo, la pratica, o ruoli sociali e culturali della matematica (compresi gli aspetti matematici di altre scienze) dai punti di vista della storia, della filosofia o delle discipline umanistiche vicine. La data di partenza è intorno al settembre 2026. Descrizione del lavoro
• Sarai responsabile della tua ricerca
• Prenderai parte alle attività accademiche e sociali della cattedra
• Sarete gradualmente integrati nelle attività didattiche nella cattedra basata sui progressi della ricerca
• Avrai accesso ai finanziamenti per la ricerca e il viaggio, una rete internazionale di collaboratori e l'ampia varietà di risorse per lo sviluppo della carriera ETH
• La lingua di lavoro è inglese
• Un colloquio attitudinale deve essere superato entro la fine del primo anno, dopo il quale la posizione è prorogata per altri tre anni Profilo
• Siete tenuti ad avere un grado MA o equivalente in un campo relativo alla vostra ricerca prima dell'inizio del vostro lavoro
• Devi progettare e gestire la tua ricerca sotto la guida dei tuoi supervisori
• Devi essere disposto a scambiare con i tuoi compagni di squadra, supportarli e imparare da loro. Sono incoraggiati argomenti, domande e metodi di ricerca non tradizionali
• Incoraggiamo anche progetti di matematica non europea, matematica commerciale o pratica, scambio matematico interculturale e progetti filosofici che considerano la matematica come pratica, piuttosto che come ideale astratto. La sedia non è un buon ambiente per progetti di filosofia analitica rigorosa, ma è aperta a progetti che integrano metodologie di filosofia analitica Luogo di lavoro Luogo di lavoro Cosa?
• La posizione è a tempo pieno (41 ore a settimana) per impostazione predefinita, ma può essere ridotta per il lavoro di cura, la salute o il benessere
• Condizioni di lavoro flessibili (orario di lavoro flessibile, possibilità di lavoro a tempo parziale, ufficio di casa)
• La scala di pagamento è disponibile qui

Visita il nostro sito Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima. Curioso? Anche noi. Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la tua domanda online entro il 31 maggio, con i seguenti documenti:
• CV con elenco delle pubblicazioni

• Una presentazione di una pagina dei tuoi interessi di ricerca tentativi, che dovrebbe essere così concentrata e concreta come puoi renderli a questo punto della tua carriera (fino a 3.500 caratteri)
• Una dichiarazione di mezza pagina (fino a 2.000 caratteri) che spiega come contribuire a migliorare il benessere, la diversità, l'inclusione e/o l'equità nel gruppo di ricerca, dipartimento, università o disciplina. Ciò può includere background, formazione, attività, ecc.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Doctoral position in the professorship of history and philosophy of mathematical sciences 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The professorship for history and philosophy of mathematical sciences , led by Prof. Roy Wagner, is a place for reflecting on all aspects of mathematical knowledge from the point of view of the humanities. Our team studies various historical and contemporary mathematical cultures from a multitude of methodological approaches. Project background We are looking for a doctoral student to conduct research on the development, practice, or social and cultural roles of mathematics (including mathematical aspects of other sciences) from the points of view of history, philosophy or neighbouring humanities disciplines. The starting date is around September 2026. Job description
• You will be in charge of your own research
• You will take part in the professorship’s academic and social activities
• You will be gradually integrated into the teaching activities in the professorship based on your research progress
• You will have access to research and travel funding, an international network of collaborators, and the wide variety of ETH career development resources
• The working language is English
• An aptitude colloquium must be passed by the end of the first year, after which the position is extended for three more years Profile
• You are required to have an MA degree or equivalent in a field related to your research before the beginning of your employment
• You must design and manage your own research under the guidance of your supervisors
• You must be willing to exchange with your fellow team members, support them, and learn from them. Non-traditional research topics, questions and methods are encouraged
• We also encourage projects on non-European mathematics, commercial or practical mathematics, cross-cultural mathematical exchange, and philosophical projects that consider mathematics as a practice, rather than as an abstract ideal. The chair is not a good environment for strict analytic philosophy projects, but is open to projects that integrate analytic philosophy methodologies Workplace Workplace We offer
• The position is full time (41 hours per week) by default, but can be reduced for care-work, health, or wellbeing
• Flexible working conditions (flexible working hours, possibility for part-time work, home office)
• The pay-scale is available here
• Training opportunities and perspectives for career development
• Support programmes (e.g. mentoring) and networks
• Commitment to diversity chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application by May 31 , with the following documents:
• CV with list of publications
• A one page summary of your MA dissertation and/or past studies trajectory (up to 3,500 characters)
• A one page presentation of your tentative research interests, which should be as focused and concrete as you can make them at this point of your career (up to 3,500 characters)
• A half page statement (up to 2,000 characters) explaining how you can contribute to improving wellbeing, diversity, inclusion and/or equity in the research group, department, university, or discipline. This may include relevant background, training, activities, etc.
• The names and contact details of 1-2 references (no reference letters are required at this stage) The appl

Descrizione Leader di gruppo nella chimica atmosferica osservazionale 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato La chimica atmosferica esplora i processi che controllano l'abbondanza e gli impatti dei gas di traccia e delle particelle di aerosol nell'atmosfera. La ricerca in questo campo è avanzata applicando una serie di metodi, tra cui studi sul campo, studi di laboratorio, telerilevamento e modellazione. Il Gruppo di Chimica atmosferica presso ETH attualmente si concentra sulla modellazione, con competenze nell'esplorazione dell'interfaccia di osservazione del modello. Questo noleggio porterà un sottogruppo complementare nella chimica atmosferica che si concentrerà sulla raccolta di nuovi vincoli osservazionali sulla composizione atmosferica. In particolare, chiediamo ai candidati con esperienza in: (1) scambio biosfera-atmosfera di gas di traccia e/o particelle (2) telerilevamento (base e/o satellite) di costituenti atmosferici di breve durata. Riteniamo inoltre che i candidati eccellenti che lavorano in altri argomenti che coinvolgono misurazioni sul campo della chimica atmosferica. Mansioni - Il Leader del Gruppo guiderà e sovrintenderà al sottogruppo di chimica atmosferica osservazionale dell'ETE - Sviluppano il proprio portafoglio scientifico e di misura - Saranno responsabili della distribuzione, dell'analisi e del mantenimento della strumentazione e della pubblicazione di risultati scientifici. Essi sovrintenderanno MS, PhD e ricercatori post-dottoriali e sono tenuti a richiedere finanziamenti esterni per sostenere gli studiosi di dottorato e post-dottorato - Il Leader del Gruppo parteciperà alle attività didattiche dell'ETE (equivalente dell'istruzione a tempo pieno di una classe all'anno)

È necessaria una certa esperienza nell'insegnamento e/o nella supervisione della ricerca - Il candidato dovrebbe evincere sia la leadership scientifica che l'indipendenza. La competenza inglese (spoken e scritto) è essenziale. Cosa? Il gruppo di chimica atmosferica è guidato dal Prof. Colette Heald e conduce ricerche esplorando i processi che controllano la composizione troposferica (gas e particelle) e la loro intersezione con il cambiamento globale. La nostra ricerca fa principalmente uso di modelli globali insieme a osservazioni sul campo e sul satellite. Questa posizione sosterrebbe l'istituzione di un sottogruppo osservazionale. Il gruppo fa parte dell'Istituto per la scienza dell'atmosfera e del clima che ospita una serie di seminari e mantiene programmi educativi ai livelli di BSc e MS. Il gruppo si trova nel campus centrale di ETH con accesso a strutture di laboratorio di alta qualità. Group Leader in Observational Atmospheric Chemistry 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken Atmospheric chemistry explores the processes controlling the abundance and impacts of trace gases and aerosol particles in the atmosphere. Research in this field is advanced by applying a range of methods, including field studies, laboratory studies, remote sensing, and modeling. The Atmospheric Chemistry Group at ETH currently focuses on modeling, with expertise in exploring the model-observation interface. This hire will lead a complementary sub-group in Atmospheric Chemistry that will focus on the collection of new observational constraints on atmospheric composition. In particular, we solicit applicants with expertise in: (1) biosphere-atmosphere exchange of trace gases and/or particles (2) remote sensing (ground-based and/or satellite) of short-lived atmospheric constituents. We will also consider excellent applicants working in other topics involving field measurements of atmospheric chemistry. Job description
• The Group Leader will lead and oversee the observational atmospheric chemistry sub-group at ETH
• They will develop their own scientific and measurement portfolio
• They will be responsible for deploying, analyzing, and maintaining instrumentation as well as publishing scientific results. They will oversee MS, PhD, and postdoctoral researchers and are expected to apply for external funding to support doctoral and postdoctoral scholars
• The Group Leader is expected to participate in teaching activities at ETH (equivalent of full-time instruction of one class per year) Profile
• Applicants should hold a PhD degree in atmospheric science or a related discipline, and have a minimum of eight years of research experience post-PhD
• It is expected that the candidate will have undertaken their doctoral and postdoctoral research in the field of atmospheric chemistry
• The candidate will have extensive experience in atmospheric chemistry measurements, including the techniques to be deployed to support their research at ETH
• The candidate will have demonstrated strong communication skills via their publication and presentation record. Some experience in teaching and/or research supervision is required
• The candidate is expected to evince both scientific leadership and independence. English proficiency (spoken and written) is essential. Employment will be according to standard regulations at ETH. The projected start date is January 2027 but can be earlier or later upon mutual agreement. The initial appointment is fixed term for 4 years, with a possibility for permanent appointment. Workplace Workplace We offer The Atmospheric Chemistry group is headed by Prof. Colette Heald and conducts research exploring the processes controlling tropospheric composition (gases and particles) and their intersection with global change. Our research primarily makes use of global models along with field and satellite observations. This position would support the establishment of an observational sub-group. The Atmospheric Chemistry group is composed of researchers from around the world and offers a friendly and supportive environment, with English as our working language. Researchers in the group work on a wide range of topics and are exposed to each others’ work through biweekly group meetings. The group is part of the Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science which hosts a seminar series and maintains educational programs at the BSc and MS levels. The group is located at ETH’s central campus with access to high quality laboratory facilities. Descrizione Chef de groupe en chimie atmosphérique observationnelle 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée La chimie atmosphérique explore les processus qui contrôlent l'abondance et les impacts des gaz traces et des particules d'aérosol dans l'atmosphère. La recherche dans ce domaine est avancée par l'application d'une série de méthodes, notamment des études de terrain, des études de laboratoire, la télédétection et la modélisation. Le Groupe de chimie atmosphérique de l'ETH se concentre actuellement sur la modélisation, avec une expertise dans l'exploration de l'interface modèle-observation. Cette embauche dirigera un sous-groupe complémentaire en chimie atmosphérique qui se concentrera sur la collecte de nouvelles contraintes d'observation sur la composition atmosphérique. En particulier, nous sollicitons des candidats ayant une expertise dans les domaines suivants : 1) échange biosphère-atmosphère de gaz traces et/ou de particules (2) télédétection (fondée sur le sol et/ou satellite) de composants atmosphériques à courte durée de vie. Nous examinerons également d'excellents candidats travaillant sur d'autres sujets concernant les mesures sur le terrain de la chimie atmosphérique. Mansioni - Le chef de groupe dirigera et supervisera le sous-groupe de la chimie atmosphérique observationnelle à l'ETH - Ils développeront leur propre portefeuille scientifique et de mesure - Ils seront responsables du déploiement, de l'analyse et de l'entretien des instruments ainsi que de la publication des résultats scientifiques. Ils superviseront les chercheurs en sciences humaines, en doctorat et en postdoctorat et devraient présenter une demande de financement externe pour appuyer les chercheurs en doctorat et en postdoctorat. - Le chef de groupe doit participer aux activités d'enseignement à l'ETH (équivalent d'un cours par an à temps plein)
• Requisiti - Les candidats doivent être titulaires d'un doctorat en sciences atmosphériques ou d'une discipline connexe et avoir au moins huit années d'expérience en recherche après le doctorat - Il est prévu que le candidat aura entrepris sa recherche doctorale et postdoctorale dans le domaine de la chimie atmosphérique - Le candidat aura une vaste expérience des mesures de la chimie atmosphérique, y compris les techniques à déployer pour soutenir sa recherche à l'ETH - Le candidat aura fait preuve de solides compétences en communication grâce à sa publication et à sa présentation. Une certaine expérience dans l'enseignement et/ou la supervision de la recherche est nécessaire - On s'attend à ce que le candidat gagne en leadership scientifique et en indépendance. La compétence en anglais (parlé et écrit) est essentielle.
• Cosa offriamo Le groupe de chimie atmosphérique est dirigé par le professeur Colette Heald et mène des recherches sur les processus qui contrôlent la composition troposphérique (gaz et particules) et leur intersection avec le changement global. Nos recherches utilisent principalement des modèles mondiaux ainsi que des observations sur le terrain et par satellite. Cette position appuierait la création d'un sous-groupe d'observation. Le groupe de chimie atmosphérique est composé de chercheurs du monde entier et offre un environnement amical et favorable, l'anglais étant notre langue de travail. Les chercheurs du groupe travaillent sur un large éventail de sujets et sont exposés les uns aux autres. Le groupe fait partie de l'Institut des sciences de l'atmosphère et du climat qui organise une série de séminaires et gère des programmes d'enseignement aux niveaux du BSc et de la MS. Le groupe est situé au campus central de l'ETH avec accès à des installations de laboratoire de haute qualité. Le chef de groupe se verra allouer cet espace de laboratoire et cet équipement pour le développement du sous-groupe de la chimie atmosphérique observationnelle. Contatto L'emploi sera conforme aux normes de l'ETH. La date de début prévue est janvier 2027, mais peut être antérieure ou ultérieure à l'accord mutuel. La nomination initiale est d ' une durée de quatre ans, avec possibilité de nomination permanente. Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca all'ETH Zurich Nous apprécions la diversité et la durabilité Conformément à nos valeurs , ETH Zurich encourage une culture inclusive. descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione post-dottorale: Mechanotyping di sistemi cellulari complessi 100%, Basilea, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Invitiamo le applicazioni per una posizione di ricerca postdoctoral focalizzata sulla mechanotyping di sistemi cellulari complessi, combinando strumenti nanotecnologici all'avanguardia, biologia cellulare avanzata e biologia quantitativa a livello di sistemi. Il progetto mira a scoprire come le proprietà meccaniche, le forze e i fenotipi fisici si integrano con le reti molecolari per regolare la funzione di sistemi cellulari complessi su più scale biologiche. Sfondo del progetto Le cellule sono sistemi meccanicamente eterogenei composti da proteine, membrane e compartimenti con proprietà fisiche distinte. Parallelamente, percepiscono continuamente e rispondono a diversi spunti meccanici dal loro ambiente, tra cui adesione, rigidità, tensione, taglio, pressione e confinamento. Questi segnali sono integrati in ampie scale spaziali e temporali, dai nanometri ai tessuti, per regolare il comportamento cellulare collettivo. La mechanobiologia cerca di capire come le cellule, i tessuti e i organoidi percepiscono, elaborano e rimodellano i segnali meccanici, e come questi processi governano funzioni biologiche fondamentali come l'omeostasi, la crescita, la differenziazione, la migrazione, lo sviluppo e l'apoptosi. Nonostante i grandi progressi, una comprensione multiscala di come le informazioni meccaniche vengono generate e integrate in sistemi multicellulari complessi rimane limitata. Il progresso nel campo richiede lo sviluppo di modelli multicellulari ingegnerizzati come sistemi di riferimento meccanico, nuovi strumenti per misurare quantitativamente e manipolare meccanica su scale, e quadri teorici per interpretare la complessità meccanobiologica. Questo progetto postdoctoral affronta queste sfide combinando sistemi di modello, probing meccanico avanzato e analisi integrativa per chiarire come le proprietà meccaniche regolano la funzione biologica a livello molecolare, cellulare e multicellulare, in ultima analisi supportando i progressi in mechanodiagnostics e mechanomedicine. Descrizione del lavoro Potrai lavorare all'interfaccia di mechanobiologia, nanotecnologia, biologia dei sistemi e biologia quantitativa, sviluppando e applicando approcci sperimentali e analitici innovativi per caratterizzare gli stati meccanici cellulari e i loro ruoli normativi. Le direzioni di ricerca includono:
• Mechanotipazione quantitativa di singole cellule, tessuti e sistemi multicellulari (ad esempio, organoidi, sferoidi)
• Sviluppo e applicazione di piattaforme nanotecnologiche per il rilevamento della forza, la manipolazione e la fenotipazione meccanica
• Tecniche biologiche avanzate delle cellule, tra cui immagini live-cell, microscopia super-risoluzione e reporter codificati geneticamente
• Sistemi di biologia approcci per integrare fenotipi meccanici con reti molecolari, di segnalazione e trascrizionali
• Modellazione quantitativa e analisi data-driven degli stati cellulari multiparametri
• Approcci ad alto rendimento e multiscala per collegare le proprietà meccaniche ai risultati cellulari funzionali La posizione offre una sostanziale libertà di modellare nuove condotte sperimentali che colmano misurazioni fisiche con un'intuizione biologica a livello di sistemi. Lavorazione indipendente su un progetto interdisciplinare impegnativo e complesso a più alti livelli scientifici presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Ingegneria dei Biosistemi, ETH Zürich di Basilea in collaborazione con gruppi leader a livello internazionale in biologia cellulare, organoide e computazionale. Profilo
• Grado di dottorato o equivalente nei settori della biologia cellulare, della mechanobiologia, della bionanotecnologia, della biologia dei sistemi, della biologia quantitativa (phenotyping), dell'analisi dei biosistemi computazionali e di altre discipline correlate
• Esperienza in biologia delle cellule umane e animali, sistemi cellulari e organoidi
• Competenza in micro-/nanofabricazione, microscopia ottica avanzata e nanooscopia, analisi delle immagini, analisi computazionale
• Interesse ad essere addestrato in biofisica molecolare e cellulare, bionanotecnologia, biologia cellulare e dei tessuti, m ottica ad alta estremità
descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Position: Mechanotyping of Complex Cellular Systems 100%, Basel, fixed-term print Drucken We invite applications for a postdoctoral research position focused on the mechanotyping of complex cellular systems, combining cutting-edge nanotechnological tools, advanced cell biology, and systems-level quantitative biology. The project aims to uncover how mechanical properties, forces, and physical phenotypes integrate with molecular networks to regulate the function of complex cellular systems across multiple biological scales. Project background Cells are mechanically heterogeneous systems composed of proteins, membranes, and compartments with distinct physical properties. In parallel, they continuously sense and respond to diverse mechanical cues from their environment, including adhesion, stiffness, tension, shear, pressure, and confinement. These cues are integrated across wide spatial and temporal scales, from nanometers to tissues, to regulate collective cellular behavior. Mechanobiology seeks to understand how cells, tissues, and organoids perceive, process, and remodel mechanical signals, and how these processes govern fundamental biological functions such as homeostasis, growth, differentiation, migration, development, and apoptosis. Despite major advances, a multiscale understanding of how mechanical information is generated and integrated in complex multicellular systems remains limited. Progress in the field requires the development of engineered multicellular models as mechanical reference systems, new tools to quantitatively measure and manipulate mechanics across scales, and theoretical frameworks to interpret mechanobiological complexity. This postdoctoral project addresses these challenges by combining model systems, advanced mechanical probing, and integrative analysis to elucidate how mechanical properties regulate biological function across molecular, cellular, and multicellular levels, ultimately supporting advances in mechanodiagnostics and mechanomedicine. Job description You will work at the interface of mechanobiology, nanotechnology, systems biology, and quantitative biology , developing and applying innovative experimental and analytical approaches to characterize cellular mechanical states and their regulatory roles. Research directions include:
• Quantitative mechanotyping of single cells, tissues, and multicellular systems (e.g., organoids, spheroids)
• Development and application of nanotechnological platforms for force sensing, manipulation, and mechanical phenotyping
• Advanced cell biological techniques, including live-cell imaging, super-resolution microscopy, and genetically encoded reporters
• Systems biology approaches to integrate mechanical phenotypes with molecular, signaling, and transcriptional networks
• Quantitative modeling and data-driven analysis of multi-parameter cellular states
• High-throughput and multi-scale approaches to link mechanical properties to functional cellular outcomes The position offers substantial freedom to shape novel experimental pipelines that bridge physical measurements with systems-level biological insight . Independent working on an interdisciplinary challenging and complex project at highest scientific levels at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering, ETH Zürich in Basel in collaboration with internationally leading groups in cell, organoid and computational biology. Profile
• PhD degree or equivalent in the fields of cell biology, mechanobiology, bionanotechnology, systems biology, quantitative biology (phenotyping), computational biosystems analysis, and other related disciplines
• Experience in human and animal cell biology, cellular systems, and organoids
• Expertise in micro-/nanofabrication, advanced optical microscopy and nanooscopy, image analysis, computational analysis
• Interest in getting trained in molecular and cellular biophysics, bionanotechnology, cell and tissue biology, high end optical m

Postdoctoral Position: Mechanotyping komplexer zellulärer Systeme 100%, Basel, befristet Drucken Drucken Wir laden Anwendungen für eine postdoctorale Forschungsposition ein, die sich auf die Mechanotypisierung komplexer zellulärer Systeme konzentriert, die innovative nanotechnologische Werkzeuge, fortschrittliche Zellbiologie und quantitative Biologie auf Systemebene kombinieren. Das Projekt zielt darauf ab, herauszufinden, wie sich mechanische Eigenschaften, Kräfte und physikalische Phänotypen in molekulare Netzwerke integrieren, um die Funktion komplexer zellulärer Systeme über mehrere biologische Skalen zu regulieren. Projekt Hintergrund Zellen sind mechanisch heterogene Systeme aus Proteinen, Membranen und Kompartimenten mit unterschiedlichen physikalischen Eigenschaften. Parallel dazu erfassen und reagieren sie kontinuierlich auf vielfältige mechanische Queues aus ihrer Umgebung, einschließlich Haftung, Steifigkeit, Spannung, Scherung, Druck und Eingrenzung. Diese Queues sind über weite räumliche und zeitliche Skalen integriert, von Nanometern bis zu Geweben, um kollektives zelluläres Verhalten zu regulieren. Die Mechanobiologie versucht zu verstehen, wie Zellen, Gewebe und Organoide mechanische Signale wahrnehmen, verarbeiten und umgestalten und wie diese Prozesse grundlegende biologische Funktionen wie Homöostase, Wachstum, Differenzierung, Migration, Entwicklung und Apoptose regeln. Trotz der großen Fortschritte bleibt ein mehrstufiges Verständnis dafür, wie mechanische Informationen erzeugt und in komplexe multizelluläre Systeme integriert werden. Fortschritte in diesem Bereich erfordern die Entwicklung von multizellulären Modellen als mechanische Referenzsysteme, neue Werkzeuge zur quantitativen Messung und Manipulation von Mechaniken über Skalen und theoretische Rahmen zur Interpretation mechanobiologischer Komplexität. Dieses postdoctorale Projekt befasst sich mit diesen Herausforderungen durch die Kombination von Modellsystemen, fortschrittlicher mechanischer Probierung und integrativer Analyse, um zu klären, wie mechanische Eigenschaften die biologische Funktion über molekulare, zelluläre und multizelluläre Ebenen regeln und letztlich Fortschritte in der Mechanodiagnostik und Mechanomedicin unterstützen. Jobbeschreibung Sie arbeiten an der Schnittstelle von Mechanobiologie, Nanotechnologie, Systembiologie und quantitativer Biologie, entwickeln und anwenden innovative experimentelle und analytische Ansätze, um zelluläre mechanische Zustände und ihre regulatorischen Rollen zu charakterisieren. Zu den Forschungsrichtungen gehören:
• Quantitative Mechanotypisierung von Einzelzellen, Geweben und multizellulären Systemen (z.B. Organoiden, Sphäroiden)
• Entwicklung und Anwendung nanotechnologischer Plattformen zur Krafterfassung, Manipulation und mechanischen Phänotypisierung
• Fortgeschrittene zellbiologische Techniken, einschließlich Live-Zell-Bildgebung, hochauflösende Mikroskopie und genetisch kodierte Reporter
• Systembiologie Ansätze zur Integration mechanischer Phänotypen mit molekularen, Signalisierungs- und Transkriptionsnetzwerken
• Quantitative Modellierung und datengesteuerte Analyse von multiparameterzellulären Zuständen
• Hochdurchsatz- und Multi-Skala-Ansätze zur Verknüpfung mechanischer Eigenschaften mit funktionellen zellulären Ergebnissen Die Position bietet erhebliche Freiheit, neue experimentelle Pipelines zu formen, die physikalische Messungen mit system-level biologischen Erkenntnissen überbrücken. Unabhängige Arbeiten an einem interdisziplinären herausfordernden und komplexen Projekt auf höchstem wissenschaftlichen Niveau am Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering, ETH Zürich in Basel in Zusammenarbeit mit international führenden Gruppen in Zell-, Organoid- und Rechenbiologie. Profil
• PhD-Abschluss oder Äquivalent in den Bereichen Zellbiologie, Mechanobiologie, Biotechnologie, Systembiologie, quantitative Biologie (Phenotyping), rechnerische Biosysteme-Analyse und andere damit verbundene Disziplinen
• Erfahrung in der Human- und Tierzellbiologie, Zellsystemen und Organoiden
• Expertise in der Mikro-/Nanofabrikation, fortschrittliche optische Mikroskopie und Nanomikroskopie, Bildanalyse, Rechenanalyse
• Interesse an der Ausbildung in molekularer und zellulärer Biophysik, Biotechnologie, Zell- und Gewebebiologie, High-End-Optik m

Position postdoctorale : Mécanotypage de systèmes cellulaires complexes 100%, Bâle, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Nous invitons à présenter des demandes pour un poste de recherche postdoctorale axé sur le mécanotypage de systèmes cellulaires complexes, combinant des outils nanotechnologiques de pointe, la biologie cellulaire avancée et la biologie quantitative de systèmes. Le projet vise à découvrir comment les propriétés mécaniques, les forces et les phénotypes physiques s'intègrent aux réseaux moléculaires pour réguler la fonction de systèmes cellulaires complexes à plusieurs échelles biologiques. Contexte du projet Les cellules sont des systèmes mécaniquement hétérogènes composés de protéines, de membranes et de compartiments ayant des propriétés physiques distinctes. En parallèle, ils sentent et réagissent continuellement à divers indices mécaniques de leur environnement, y compris l'adhérence, la rigidité, la tension, le cisaillement, la pression et le confinement. Ces repères sont intégrés à de larges échelles spatiales et temporelles, des nanomètres aux tissus, pour réguler le comportement cellulaire collectif. La méchanobiologie cherche à comprendre comment les cellules, les tissus et les organoïdes perçoivent, traitent et remodelent les signaux mécaniques, et comment ces processus régissent les fonctions biologiques fondamentales telles que l'homéostasie, la croissance, la différenciation, la migration, le développement et l'apoptose. Malgré des progrès importants, une compréhension à plusieurs échelles de la façon dont l'information mécanique est générée et intégrée dans des systèmes multicellulaires complexes demeure limitée. Le progrès sur le terrain exige le développement de modèles multicellulaires conçus comme systèmes de référence mécanique, de nouveaux outils pour mesurer quantitativement et manipuler la mécanique à travers les échelles, et de cadres théoriques pour interpréter la complexité méchanobiologique. Ce projet postdoctoral répond à ces défis en combinant des systèmes modèles, une analyse mécanique avancée et une analyse intégrative afin d'élucider la façon dont les propriétés mécaniques régulent la fonction biologique à tous les niveaux moléculaire, cellulaire et multicellulaire, soutenant finalement les progrès en mécanodiagnostique et en mécanomédecine. Description du poste Vous travaillerez à l'interface de la mécanisation, de la nanotechnologie, de la biologie des systèmes et de la biologie quantitative, en développant et en appliquant des approches expérimentales et analytiques novatrices pour caractériser les états mécaniques cellulaires et leurs rôles réglementaires. Les orientations de recherche comprennent :
• Mécanotypage quantitatif de cellules, tissus et systèmes multicellulaires uniques (par exemple, organoides, sphéroïdes)
• Développement et application de plates-formes nanotechnologiques pour la détection de force, la manipulation et le phénotypage mécanique
• Techniques biologiques cellulaires avancées, y compris l'imagerie des cellules vivantes, la microscopie à super résolution et les reporters génétiquement codés
• Approches de biologie des systèmes pour intégrer les phénotypes mécaniques aux réseaux moléculaires, de signalisation et de transcription
• Modélisation quantitative et analyse basée sur les données des états cellulaires multiparamètres
• Approches à haut débit et à plusieurs échelles pour lier les propriétés mécaniques aux résultats cellulaires fonctionnels La position offre une grande liberté de façonner de nouveaux pipelines expérimentaux qui relient les mesures physiques avec des aperçus biologiques au niveau des systèmes. Indépendant travaillant sur un projet interdisciplinaire difficile et complexe aux plus hauts niveaux scientifiques du Département des sciences et de l'ingénierie des biosystèmes, ETH Zürich à Bâle, en collaboration avec des groupes de premier plan internationaux en biologie cellulaire, organolytique et computationnelle. Profil
• Doctorat ou équivalent dans les domaines de la biologie cellulaire, de la méchanobiologie, de la biotechnologie, de la biologie des systèmes, de la biologie quantitative (phénotypage), de l'analyse des biosystèmes informatiques et d'autres disciplines connexes
• Expérience en biologie des cellules humaines et animales, systèmes cellulaires et organoides
• Expertise en micro/nanofabrication, microscopie optique avancée et nanooscopie, analyse d'images, analyse informatique
• Intérêt pour une formation en biophysique moléculaire et cellulaire, en bionanotechnologie, en biologie cellulaire et tissulaire, en optique de pointe

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Laboratory Technician (Assistente Tecnico) in RNA Biologia e Meccanismi Malattiali 80%-100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Il laboratorio di biologia e malattia RNA presso l'Istituto di Biologia Molecolare e Biofisica (Dipartimento di Biologia), ETH Zurich, invita applicazioni per un laboratorio di ricerca quotidiana. Il laboratorio studia la regolazione genica dei mammiferi e le vie di elaborazione del RNA. I progetti si basano su una combinazione di saggi strutturali, biochimici e cellulari, tra cui crio-elettrone e microscopia leggera, editing genico, sequenziamento di prossima generazione, proteomica e ricostituzione di grandi complessi proteici-RNA da proteine ricombinanti. Utilizzando questi strumenti il laboratorio mira a determinare la base molecolare del meccanismo delle malattie al fine di trovare nuovi obiettivi per il trattamento. Descrizione del lavoro Il gruppo di ricerca è alla ricerca di un collaboratore aperto e flessibile. Il vostro lavoro nell'organizzazione di laboratorio aiuterà a mantenere il laboratorio senza intoppi, mentre la vostra collaborazione impegnata sosterrà l'avanzamento dei nostri diversi progetti di ricerca. Come candidato di successo, sarai un membro attivo del laboratorio e parteciperai ai compiti e alle responsabilità generali del laboratorio. I compiti principali includono lavorare a stretto contatto con altri membri del laboratorio per assistere i loro progetti, regolando in modo flessibile la domanda. Nello specifico, si sta effettuando esperimenti da clonazione di costrutti ad espressione proteica e purificazione da cellule batteriche e insetti. Potrai coltivare le linee cellulari della cultura dei tessuti mammiferi, trasformarli per esperimenti, generare linee cellulari stabili e analizzare i modelli di espressione come ad esempio immunofluorescenza, blotting occidentale o RT-qPCR. Potrai documentare diligentemente il tuo lavoro di laboratorio compreso il mantenimento e l'aggiornamento di database interni. Inoltre, sarete responsabili di organizzare e coordinare in modo indipendente le riparazioni e la manutenzione di attrezzature di laboratorio. Laboratory Technician (Technical Assistant) in RNA Biology and Disease Mechanisms 80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The RNA Biology and Disease laboratory at the Institute of Molecular Biology and Biophysics (Department of Biology), ETH Zurich, invites applications for a laboratory technician to support its daily research activities and laboratory operations. The lab studies mammalian gene regulation and RNA processing pathways. Projects rely on a combination of structural, biochemical and cellular assays, including cryo-electron and light microscopy, gene editing, next-generation sequencing, proteomics and reconstitution of large protein-RNA complexes from recombinant proteins. Using these tools the laboratory aims to determine the molecular basis of disease mechanism in order to find novel targets for treatment. Job description The research group is looking for an open-minded and flexible co-worker. Your work in lab organisation will help to keep the lab running smoothly, while your committed collaboration will support the advancement of our diverse research projects. As a successful candidate, you will be an active member of the lab and participate in general lab duties and responsibilities. Core tasks include working closely with other lab members to assist their projects, adjusting flexibly to demand. Specifically, you will be carrying out experiments from cloning of constructs to protein expression and purification from bacterial and insect cells. You will culture mammalian tissue culture cell lines, transform them for experiments, generate stable cell lines, and analyse expression patterns e.g.by immunofluorescence, western blotting or RT-qPCR. You will diligently document your lab work including maintaining and updating internal databases. Moreover, you will be responsible to independently organise and coordinate repairs and maintenance of laboratory equipment. The position is available as of 1.6.2026 or by agreement and initially limited to one year with a possible longer-term perspective contingent on funding availability. Profile
• You have completed an apprenticeship as a laboratory technician, or hold a Master's degree in biochemistry, biology or related fields.
• You have experience in molecular and cell biological, as well as biochemical methods, ideally also in handling RNA.
• Your independent working style and flexibility allow you to support various research projects.
• Your willingness to learn new techniques is high and you like to work precisely.
• You use your initiative and organisational skills to improve daily lab work.
• Fluency in both spoken and written English is required. Good German language skills are desirable. Workplace Workplace We offer
• A stimulating position in a welcoming, motivated, international team, which performs fundamental biochemical research.

Ricercatore post-dottorato: Stimolazione idraulica e comportamento proppant in roccia cristallina 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Ingegneria Geologia e il BedrettoLab all'ETH di Zurigo invita le applicazioni per una posizione Postdoctoral Researcher all'interno del progetto europeo di ricerca UPLIFT, concentrandosi sulle tecnologie di stimolazione idraulica eco-compatibile nelle formazioni cristalline della roccia. La posizione si basa sull'ETH di Zurigo e coinvolge ricerche sperimentali presso il Laboratorio sotterraneo di Bedretto. La stimolazione idraulica è una tecnologia chiave per migliorare la permeabilità nei serbatoi geotermici. Mentre la stimolazione multistadio con proppants e additivi chimici è ampiamente applicata nell'industria del petrolio e del gas, la sua accettazione in Europa rimane limitata a causa delle preoccupazioni ambientali. Gli approcci di stimolazione dell'acqua sono più comunemente accettati, ma la loro efficacia rispetto ai metodi a base di proppant in particolare nella roccia cristallina rimane insufficientemente compresa. Il Bedretto Underground Laboratory offre un ambiente unico e altamente strumentale per indagare i processi siero-idro-termo-meccanici accoppiati durante la stimolazione idraulica. All'interno del progetto UPLIFT, saranno condotti esperimenti di laboratorio e di campo controllati per valutare solo le tecniche di stimolazione a base di proppanto e chimicamente assistita. L'obiettivo è quello di sviluppare strategie di stimolazione sicure, efficienti e ecologiche per applicazioni geotermiche in tutta Europa. Descrizione del lavoro

descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Researcher: Hydraulic stimulation and proppant behaviour in crystalline rock 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Engineering Geology and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position within the European research project UPLIFT, focusing on environmentally friendly hydraulic stimulation technologies in crystalline rock formations. The position is based at ETH Zurich and involves experimental research at the Bedretto Underground Laboratory. Hydraulic stimulation is a key technology for enhancing permeability in geothermal reservoirs. While multi-stage stimulation using proppants and chemical additives is widely applied in the oil and gas industry, its acceptance in Europe remains limited due to environmental concerns. Water-only stimulation approaches are more commonly accepted, yet their effectiveness compared to proppant-based methods particularly in crystalline rock remains insufficiently understood. The Bedretto Underground Laboratory provides a unique, highly instrumented environment to investigate coupled seismo-hydro-thermo-mechanical processes during hydraulic stimulation. Within the UPLIFT project, controlled laboratory and field-scale experiments will be conducted to evaluate water-only, proppant-based, and chemically assisted stimulation techniques. The goal is to develop safe, efficient, and environmentally acceptable stimulation strategies for geothermal applications across Europe. Job description
• Plan, conduct and analyse hydraulic stimulation experiments including proppant in vertical and horizontal boreholes (30–120 m scale) to investigate proppant transport, placement efficiency, and interaction with natural fracture networks
• Assess the effectiveness of different stimulation strategies and proppant placement approaches under varying geological conditions in terms of permeability enhancement and fracture geometry
• Collaborate with project partners performing small-scale laboratory experiments (GFZ) regarding joint interpretations and recommendations for the design full-scale hydraulic stimulation operations (e.g., Litoměřice site and other European contexts)
• Contribute to project deliverables and reporting, publish results in peer-reviewed journals and present findings at international conferences
• Collaborate closely with project UPLIFT partners (GFZ, various industry partners) and support coordination between experimental, modelling, and field activities Profile
• PhD in Engineeing Geology, Geophysics, Geomechanics, Earth Sciences, Physics, Engineering, or a related field
• Strong background in rock mechanics, hydrogeology, or reservoir engineering
• Experience with laboratory experiments and/or fieldwork in subsurface environments
• Willingness to participate in underground field campaigns
• Skills in numerical modelling (e.g., fracture mechanics, fluid flow)
• Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, MATLAB, or similar)
• Experience with seismic or fibre-optic sensing data is an asset
• Ability to work independently and lead research tasks within a collaborative environment
• Excellent communication skills in English Workplace Workplace We offer
• A fully funded postdoctoral position (initially 2 years, with possible extension)
• Employment according to ETH Zurich regulations

• A dynamic, interdisciplinary and international research environment with strong links to academia and industry

Chercheur postdoctoral : stimulation hydraulique et comportement de propane dans la roche cristalline 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken La Chaire de géologie de l'ingénierie et le BedrettoLab de l'ETH Zurich invitent les chercheurs postdoctoraux au sein du projet européen UPLIFT, axé sur les technologies de stimulation hydraulique respectueuses de l'environnement dans les formations de roches cristallines. Le poste est basé à l'ETH Zurich et implique des recherches expérimentales au Laboratoire souterrain de Bedretto. La stimulation hydraulique est une technologie clé pour améliorer la perméabilité des réservoirs géothermiques. Bien que la stimulation en plusieurs étapes à l'aide de proppants et d'additifs chimiques soit largement appliquée dans l'industrie pétrolière et gazière, son acceptation en Europe reste limitée en raison de préoccupations environnementales. Les approches de stimulation de l'eau uniquement sont plus communément acceptées, mais leur efficacité par rapport aux méthodes basées sur le propant, en particulier dans les roches cristallines, reste insuffisamment comprise. Le Bedretto Underground Laboratory offre un environnement unique et hautement instrumenté pour étudier les processus sismo-hydro-thermo-mécaniques couplés pendant la stimulation hydraulique. Dans le cadre du projet UPLIFT, des expériences contrôlées en laboratoire et sur le terrain seront menées afin d'évaluer les techniques de stimulation à base d'eau, de propant et d'aide chimique. L'objectif est de mettre au point des stratégies de stimulation sûres, efficaces et écologiques pour les applications géothermiques en Europe. Description du poste
• Planifier, réaliser et analyser des expériences de stimulation hydraulique incluant le propane dans les forages verticaux et horizontaux (30 à 120 m d'échelle) pour étudier le transport du propane, l'efficacité de placement et l'interaction avec les réseaux naturels de fracture
• Évaluer l'efficacité des différentes stratégies de stimulation et des approches de positionnement des propanes dans des conditions géologiques variables en termes d'amélioration de la perméabilité et de géométrie des fractures
• Collaborer avec des partenaires de projet effectuant des expériences de laboratoire à petite échelle (GFZ) concernant des interprétations conjointes et des recommandations pour la conception d'opérations de stimulation hydraulique à grande échelle (par exemple site Litoměřice et autres contextes européens)

La sismicità indotta nei sistemi geotermici spesso continua dopo l'iniezione o la produzione viene arrestata, un fenomeno noto come post-shut-in o la sismicità trailing. descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD Position: Optimization of shut-in strategies to reduce induced seismicity 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Engineering Geology and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a PhD position within a research project on poroelastic effects and induced seismicity in geothermal systems. The position focuses on post-shut-in seismicity and the design of safer operational protocols. Induced seismicity in geothermal systems often continues after injection or production is stopped, a phenomenon known as post-shut-in or trailing seismicity. In many cases, the largest seismic events occur after shut-in, posing challenges for hazard mitigation and operational safety. Despite extensive modelling efforts, the governing mechanisms are still not fully understood, and field observations of pressure and deformation during shut-in, that may improve our process understanding, are rare. This project exploits the unique monitoring capabilities of the Bedretto Underground Laboratory to investigate these processes and to develop experimentally validated guidelines for safer shut-in strategies. Job description
• Investigate pressure, deformation, and seismicity data from hydraulic stimulation experiments to derive conceptual models of post-shut-in processes
• Develop hydromechanical models to reproduce observed shut-in behaviour and test competing hypotheses (e.g., pressure diffusion vs. poroelastic effects)
• Develop/apply earthquake source physics models to understand induced seismicity processe
• Design and execute controlled hydraulic stimulation and production experiments with different shut-in protocols
• Quantify how different shut-in strategies influence seismicity rates and magnitudes
• Derive recommendations for optimized shut-in procedures to minimize induced seismic hazard
• Publish results, present at conferences, and contribute to project reporting Profile
• MSc degree in Engineering Geology, Geophysics, Seismology, Earth Sciences, Physics, Engineering, or a related field
• Interest in induced seismicity, geomechanics, and field experiments
• Strong quantitative and analytical skills
• Interest in learning complex numerical modelling tools
• Programming skills (Python and/or matlab required)
• Willingness to participate in underground field campaigns
• Ability to work in an interdisciplinary and collaborative environment
• Strong communication skills in English (German and/or French is a plus) Workplace Workplace We offer
• A fully funded PhD position (up to 4 years)
• Employment according to ETH Zurich regulations
• Access to the Bedretto Underground Laboratory
• A collaborative environment bridging research, field experiments, and real-world applications
• Opportunities for publications and international conference participation Supervision and Environment The PhD student will be hosted at the Chair of Engineering Geology at ETH Zurich and will closely collaborate with a multidisciplinary research teams of the Swiss Seismological Service and the BedrettoLab. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . Curious? So are we. La position est axée sur la sismicité après l'arrivée et la conception de protocoles opérationnels plus sûrs. La sismicité induite dans les systèmes géothermiques se poursuit souvent après l'arrêt de l'injection ou de la production, un phénomène connu sous le nom de sismicité post-fuite ou de sismicité traînante. Dans de nombreux cas, les événements sismiques les plus importants se produisent après la fermeture, ce qui pose des défis pour l'atténuation des risques et la sécurité opérationnelle. Malgré de nombreux efforts de modélisation, les mécanismes directeurs ne sont toujours pas pleinement compris, et les observations sur le terrain de la pression et de la déformation pendant le verrouillage, qui peuvent améliorer notre compréhension du processus, sont rares. Ce projet exploite les capacités de surveillance uniques du Laboratoire souterrain de Bedretto pour étudier ces processus et élaborer des lignes directrices validées expérimentalement pour des stratégies de fermeture plus sûres. Description de travail

• Développer des modèles hydromécaniques pour reproduire le comportement de fermeture observé et tester des hypothèses concurrentes (p. ex. diffusion de la pression par rapport aux effets poroélastiques)

• Formuler des recommandations pour optimiser les procédures de fermeture afin de minimiser les risques sismiques induits
