Postdoc position: Production-induced seismicity in fractured reservoirs 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Swiss Seismological Service (SED) and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position within a two-year research project on poroelastic effects and induced seismicity in geothermal systems. The position focuses on production-induced seismicity in fractured reservoirs and combines field experiments, data analysis, and numerical modelling. Project background Geothermal energy projects can induce seismicity during both fluid injection and fluid production through by complex hydromechanical processes in fractured rock. Development of simple and standardized modelling approaches to assess production-induced seismicity would benefit from insitu observations to identify relevant or missing hydromechanical processes and to calibrate models with. The project leverages the unique infrastructure of the Bedretto Underground Laboratory, where dense multiparametric monitoring networks provide unprecedented observations of pressure, deformation, and seismicity. The project aims at validating modelling approaches and practical workflows for assessing seismic hazard related to fluid production in Swiss geothermal projects (e.g. in Vaud and Geneva). Job description
• Analyse high-resolution pressure, deformation, and seismic datasets from past and new production experiments to identify governing hydromechanical processes
• Develop and apply coupled hydromechanical models (continuum and discontinuum) to reproduce observed behaviour and quantify poroelastic effects in fractured reservoirs
• Develop and apply earthquake source physics models to understand processes underlying induced seismicity
• Plan and conduct controlled production experiments at the BedrettoLab to test hypotheses and validate models
• Translate modelling results into simplified and scalable workflows for assessing production-induced seismicity in geothermal projects
• Apply developed methods to realistic geothermal scenarios (e.g., Swiss hydrothermal systems) and contribute to best-practice guidelines
• Publish results in peer-reviewed journals, present at conferences, and collaborate with academic, governmental, and industry stakeholders Profile
• PhD in Geophysics, Geomechanics, Earth Sciences, Physics, Engineering, or a related field
• Strong background in hydromechanics, reservoir modelling, induced seismicity, earthquake source physics
• Experience with numerical modelling tools (e.g., MOOSE, PorePy, or similar)
• Programming skills (Python, MATLAB, or similar)
• Experience with field data and/or underground experiments is an advantage
• Ability to work independently and lead research activities
• Strong analytical and communication skills in English (German or French is a plus) Workplace Workplace We offer
• A fully funded postdoctoral position (initially 2 years, with possible extension)
• Employment according to ETH Zurich regulations
• Access to the Bedretto Underground Laboratory, a world-leading research infrastructure
• A highly interdisciplinary environment bridging geophysics, geomechanics, energy research and earthquake physics
• Opportunities to lead publications and develop an independent research profile
• Close collaboration with ETH Zurich, the Swiss Seismological Service, and external stakeholders such as Swiss Federal Office of Energy, Canton de Genève, Canton de Vaud Supervision and Environment The position is jointly hosted by the Swiss Seismological Service (SED) at ETH Zurich in close collaboration with the BedrettoLab and the Chair of Engineering Geology. The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with experts in hydromechanics, induced seismicity, geothermal energy and earthquake source physics, and will interact with ongoing national and international projects. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainabi

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Machine Learning Scientist (AI-based Weather Forecasting) 100%, Locarno, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Recenti progressi nella previsione meteo basata su AI hanno dimostrato notevole abilità ed efficienza computazionale. Tuttavia, la maggior parte degli attuali sistemi di previsione meteorologica (MLWP) si basano principalmente sulle analisi NWP per l'inizializzazione e sfruttano solo parzialmente la ricchezza delle osservazioni satellitari disponibili. Con l'avvento della Meteosat Third Generation (MTG), nuove misurazioni ad alta frequenza e ad alta risoluzione di nuvole, umidità, temperatura e attività fulmine offrono opportunità senza precedenti per migliorare notevolmente le previsioni regionali. Nell'ambito di un Research Fellowship supportato da EUMETSAT, stiamo promuovendo l'integrazione delle osservazioni satellitari geostazionarie in un sistema MLWP regionale di nuova generazione. Il progetto si basa su un modello di previsione regionale a base di grafici esistente, allungato-grigliato sviluppato a MeteoSwiss ed è incorporato nel quadro Anemoi avviato da ECMWF. L'obiettivo è quello di sviluppare e valutare nuove architetture multi-encoder-decoder in grado di ingerire vari flussi di dati satellitari (ad esempio radiances, prodotti cloud, osservazioni fulmine, suoni iperspectral) e integrarli in cicli di previsione ad alta frequenza con tempi di piombo da corto raggio a 10 giorni in anticipo. Il lavoro sarà svolto in stretta collaborazione con partner nazionali e internazionali e contribuirà direttamente al futuro sfruttamento operativo dei dati MTG. Descrizione del lavoro Stiamo cercando un programmatore scientifico / sviluppatore di software per unire il nostro team motivato e interdisciplinare.
• Sviluppare e implementare architetture di modelli di apprendimento automatico che consentano l'ingestione diretta dei dati satellitari di prossima generazione (ad esempio MTG FCI, LI, IRS) in modelli di previsione regionali all'avanguardia in Anemoi
• Contribuire all'evoluzione di un framework multi-encoder-decoder MLWP all'interno dell'ecosistema Anemoi Apprezziamo le persone che amano risolvere problemi complessi, collaborare attraverso le discipline, e contribuire in diverse fasi del flusso di lavoro come il sistema matura. Si tratta di un contratto a tempo determinato di 1 anno, con la possibilità di proroga fino a 2 anni aggiuntivi. Il posto di lavoro principale si trova a MeteoSwiss Locarno-Monti con visite regolari a Zurigo. L'importo della retribuzione sarà conforme al sistema salariale di ETH Zürich. Profilo Accogliamo le domande dei candidati con sfondi diversi che soddisfano la maggior parte (non necessariamente tutti) dei seguenti criteri:
• PhD in informatica, scienza dei dati, scienze naturali (ad esempio fisica, meteorologia) o un campo correlato.
• Esperienza di lavoro con dati satellitari (ad esempio osservazioni geostazionarie, radiances, prodotti di recupero)
• Forte capacità di programmazione in Python
• Esperienza nell'apprendimento automatico, idealmente comprese architetture di apprendimento profonde come reti neurali di grafico, trasformatori, o modelli spatio-temporali
• Esperienza con ambienti di calcolo ad alte prestazioni o distribuiti
• Buona comprensione dei processi meteorologici e dei modelli numerici
descriptionByLocale.en:
Machine Learning Scientist (AI-based Weather Forecasting) 100%, Locarno, fixed-term print Drucken Recent advances in AI-based weather prediction have demonstrated remarkable skill and computational efficiency. However, most current machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP) systems rely primarily on NWP analyses for initialization and only partially exploit the wealth of available satellite observations. With the advent of the Meteosat Third Generation (MTG), new high-frequency and high-resolution measurements of clouds, moisture, temperature, and lightning activity provide unprecedented opportunities for substantially improving regional forecasts. Project background Within the framework of a Research Fellowship supported by EUMETSAT, we are advancing the integration of geostationary satellite observations into a next-generation regional MLWP system. The project builds on an existing graph-based, stretched-grid regional forecasting model developed at MeteoSwiss and is embedded in the Anemoi framework initiated by ECMWF. The objective is to develop and evaluate novel multi-encoder-decoder architectures capable of ingesting various satellite data streams (e.g. radiances, cloud products, lightning observations, hyperspectral soundings) and integrating them into high-frequency forecasting cycles with lead times from short-range to up to 10 days ahead. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with national and international partners and contributes directly to the future operational exploitation of MTG data. Job description We are looking for a Scientific Programmer / Software Developer to join our motivated and interdisciplinary team. In this role, you will:
• Develop and implement machine-learning model architectures enabling the direct ingestion of next generation satellite data (e.g. MTG FCI, LI, IRS) into state-of-the-art regional forecasting models in Anemoi
• Contribute to the evolution of a multi-encoder-decoder MLWP framework within the Anemoi ecosystem
• Train, fine-tune, and evaluate models using large-scale meteorological and satellite datasets
• Quantify the impact of satellite data on forecast skill across variables and lead times
• Collaborate closely with scientists, ML researchers, and operational forecasting teams to ensure that forecast outputs meet the needs of diverse users
• Disseminate results through scientific publications, conference presentations, and exchanges with EUMETSAT and partner institutions We value people who enjoy solving complex problems, collaborating across disciplines, and contributing across different stages of the workflow as the system matures. This is a fixed-term contract of 1 year, with the possibility of extension for up to an additional 2 years. The main workplace is located at MeteoSwiss Locarno-Monti with regular visits to Zürich. The amount of remuneration will be in accordance with the salary system of ETH Zürich. Profile We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds who meet most (not necessarily all) of the following criteria:
• PhD in computer science, data science, natural sciences (e.g. physics, meteorology) or a related field. Candidates with an MSc and proven professional experience may also be considered
• Experience working with satellite data (e.g. geostationary observations, radiances, retrieval products)
• Strong programming skills in Python
• Experience in machine learning, ideally including deep learning architectures such as graph neural networks, transformers, or spatio-temporal models
• Experience with high-performance or distributed computing environments
• Good understanding of meteorological processes and numerical weather prediction
• Interest in DevOps practices and sustainable software engineering
• Ability to work independently on research questions while contributing to a collaborative team environment
• Motivation to work in a diverse, interdisciplinary, and international environment •

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Student Research Assistant – Sviluppo e assemblaggio di strumenti per la ricerca atmosferica 10%-30%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Il gruppo di Fisica atmosferica dell'ETH Zurigo sta cercando un Assistente per la Ricerca Studente per sostenere lo sviluppo e l'assemblaggio di strumenti utilizzati durante le campagne sul campo . Il nostro gruppo di ricerca studia il ruolo cruciale delle nuvole e degli aerosol nel sistema climatico, mirando a comprendere meglio come i processi microfisici cloud spingano sia la formazione delle precipitazioni che l'impatto radiativo delle nuvole. Sfondo del progetto Questo ruolo supporta direttamente i nostri sforzi di ricerca costruendo gli strumenti che distribuiamo nel settore. Lo strumento primario è un imager olografico personalizzato sviluppato nel nostro gruppo. Utilizza olografia a percorso aperto in linea per catturare immagini 2D di particelle di nube in un volume ben definito. Con questo possiamo ricostruire la posizione, la forma e la dimensione delle gocce di nube come piccole come 5.5 µm e cristalli di ghiaccio fino a diversi millimetri. Il nostro ultimo sviluppo è una versione leggera di nome HOLIMOAir. Con due unità già completate, il piano è quello di costruire ulteriori 2–3 unità entro la fine dell'anno. Questo include fare adattamenti per garantire che siano adatti per le misurazioni del tunnel eolico e la distribuzione nell'Antartico.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Student Research Assistant – Development and assembly of instruments for atmospheric research 10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Atmospheric Physics group at ETH Zurich is looking for a Student Research Assistant to support the development and assembly of instruments used during field campaigns . Our research group studies the crucial role of clouds and aerosols in the climate system, aiming to better understand how cloud microphysical processes drive both precipitation formation and the radiative impact of clouds. Project background This role directly supports our research efforts by building the instruments we deploy in the field. The primary instrument is a custom holographic imager developed within our group. It uses in-line open-path holography to capture 2D images of cloud particles in a well-defined volume. With this we can reconstruct the position, shape, and size of cloud droplets as small as 5.5 µm and ice crystals up to several millimeters. Our latest development is a lightweight version named HOLIMOAir. With two units already completed, the plan is to build an additional 2–3 units by the end of the year. This includes making adaptations to ensure they are suitable for wind tunnel measurements and deployment in the Antarctic. Job description
• Building further HOLIMOAir units and develop upgrades for other instrumentation
• Mechanical assembly of instrument housing and optical components
• Soldering of cable assemblies and PCBs, testing of electronics
• Upgrading of sofware running on instrumentation
• Support instrument integration, calibration, and field campaign preparation
• Assist with maintenance and basic documentation Profile
• Enrolled student at ETH Zurich or another Swiss university
• Background or strong interest in mechatronics, optics, electronics with hands-on experience
• Manual dexterity and careful working style, workshop and/or electronics experience is a plus
• Basic python programming skills, linux command line experience a plus
• Interest in experimental or field-based research Workplace Workplace We offer
• Direct involvement in cutting-edge atmospheric research
• Flexible working hours (10–15 h/week during semester, possibility for more during breaks)
• Standard ETH student assistant salary
• Opportunity for a long-term engagement (≥1 year) chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application, including the following documents:
• A short motivation letter (max. 1 page) highlighting your relevant experience and interest in the position
• Your current Curriculum Vitae (CV) Review of applications will start May 8th and continue until the position is filled. The preferred start date is as soon as possible. For any questions related to the project or this position, please contact Dr. Jan Henneberger (jan.henneberger@env.ethz.ch). L'obiettivo primario è quello di favorire l'interazione tra circa 150 membri ZNZ, gruppi di ricerca basati su ETHZ, UZH e i quattro ospedali universitari, nella ricerca e nella formazione di neuroscienze. Ciò include lo sviluppo di infrastrutture innovative, il finanziamento per progetti collaborativi, la promozione della traduzione dei risultati della ricerca nella pratica clinica, la costruzione e il mantenimento dei rapporti con altri centri di ricerca in Svizzera e a livello internazionale, e la valorizzazione della consapevolezza pubblica dei risultati dei membri ZNZ. Il Direttore Generale lavora a stretto contatto con il comitato direttivo ZNZ, responsabile della strategia generale del centro. Sfondo del progetto Il paesaggio della ricerca di neuroscienze all'interno della rete ZNZ è vario. I ricercatori provenienti da sfondi tra cui biologia, medicina, psicologia, biochimica, fisica, ingegneria, informatica e economia indagano domande fondamentali su come il cervello funziona in salute e malattia. Questo spinge lo sviluppo di nuove tecnologie diagnostiche, terapie e “intelligenti”. Negli ultimi anni, i membri ZNZ hanno contribuito in modo significativo ai progressi nelle terapie per la demenza, la sclerosi multipla e le lesioni del midollo spinale, così come per le tecnologie di neuroriabilitazione, l'imaging cerebrale all'avanguardia, le applicazioni ad ultrasuoni focalizzate, la ricerca sul sonno, le neuroeconomia e le reti neurali artificiali. Descrizione del lavoro Il Direttore Generale opera in gran parte in modo indipendente e si assume una significativa responsabilità per il successo complessivo del Centro. Poiché il ruolo comporta un'interazione continua con un'ampia gamma di stakeholder, porta un alto livello di visibilità. La soluzione dei problemi attraverso più consiglieri può essere complessa e richiede un forte coordinamento e giudizio.

ZNZ Managing Director 80%-100%, Zurich, permanent print Drucken The Managing Director is responsible for implementing the objectives of the Neuroscience Center Zurich (ZNZ), a highly interdisciplinary research network jointly supported by ETH Zurich (ETHZ) and the University of Zurich (UZH). The primary goal is to foster interaction among approximately 150 ZNZ members—research groups based at ETHZ, UZH, and the four university hospitals—in neuroscience research and training. This includes developing innovative infrastructure, securing funding for collaborative projects, promoting the translation of research findings into clinical practice, building and maintaining relationships with other research centers in Switzerland and internationally, and enhancing public awareness of the achievements of ZNZ members. The Managing Director works closely with the ZNZ Steering Committee, which is responsible for the center’s overall strategy. Project background The landscape of neuroscience research within the ZNZ network is diverse. Researchers from backgrounds including biology, medicine, psychology, biochemistry, physics, engineering, computer science, and economics investigate fundamental questions about how the brain functions in health and disease. This drives the development of new diagnostics, therapies, and “intelligent” technologies. In recent years, ZNZ members have contributed significantly to advances in therapies for dementia, multiple sclerosis, and spinal cord injury, as well as to neurorehabilitation technologies, state-of-the-art brain imaging, focused ultrasound applications, sleep research, neuroeconomics, and artificial neural networks. Job description The Managing Director operates largely independently and bears significant responsibility for the overall success of the Center. As the role involves continuous interaction with a wide range of stakeholders it carries a high level of visibility. Problem-solving across multiple advisory boards can be complex and requires strong coordination and judgment. The Managing Director leads a small team and is responsible for:
• Promoting scientific collaboration among ZNZ research groups
• Providing organizational and financial support for selected ZNZ projects
• Maintaining and strengthening relationships with external research partners
• Managing ZNZ PhD grants and coordinating travel support for students
• Directing the International PhD Program in Neuroscience at UZH and ETH Zurich
• Overseeing the Specialized Master’s Program in Interdisciplinary Brain Sciences at UZH and ETH Zurich
• Leading communication with stakeholders, including newsletters, social media, and public events
• Participating in steering committees of related units at UZH
• Organizing regular events for ZNZ members, such as annual symposia and strategy meetings Profile
• PhD in natural sciences, engineering, or a related field
• Several years of postdoctoral or relevant professional experience
• Experience or knowledge in neuroscience or a related discipline
• Professional experience in clinical settings and/or the biotech/medtech industry is an advantage
• Established professional network in neuroscience, health, biotech, or medtech

• Excellent communication skills and a passion for interdisciplinary collaboration

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht ZNZ Geschäftsführer 80%-100%, Zürich, permanente Drucken Der Geschäftsführer ist verantwortlich für die Umsetzung der Ziele des Neuroscience Center Zürich (ZNZ), eines hochinterdisziplinären Forschungsnetzwerks, das gemeinsam von der ETH Zürich (ETHZ) und der Universität Zürich (UZH) unterstützt wird. Das primäre Ziel ist es, die Interaktion zwischen etwa 150 ZNZ-Mitgliedern zu fördern – Forschungsgruppen mit ETHZ, UZH und den vier Universitätskliniken – in der neurowissenschaftlichen Forschung und Ausbildung. Dazu gehören die Entwicklung innovativer Infrastrukturen, die Finanzierung von Kooperationsprojekten, die Förderung der Übersetzung von Forschungsergebnissen in die klinische Praxis, der Aufbau und Pflege von Beziehungen zu anderen Forschungszentren in der Schweiz und international sowie die Sensibilisierung der Öffentlichkeit für die Leistungen der ZNZ-Mitglieder. Der Geschäftsführer arbeitet eng mit dem ZNZ Lenkungsausschuss zusammen, der für die Gesamtstrategie des Zentrums verantwortlich ist. Projekt Hintergrund Die Landschaft der neurowissenschaftlichen Forschung im ZNZ-Netzwerk ist vielfältig. Forscher aus Hintergründen wie Biologie, Medizin, Psychologie, Biochemie, Physik, Ingenieurwesen, Informatik und Wirtschaft untersuchen grundlegende Fragen, wie das Gehirn in Gesundheit und Krankheit funktioniert. Dies treibt die Entwicklung neuer Diagnostik, Therapien und „intelligenter“ Technologien voran. L'objectif principal est de favoriser l'interaction entre environ 150 membres de ZNZ – groupes de recherche basés à ETHZ, UZH et les quatre hôpitaux universitaires – en recherche et formation en neurosciences. Il s'agit notamment de développer des infrastructures innovantes, d'obtenir des fonds pour des projets collaboratifs, de promouvoir la traduction des résultats de la recherche en pratique clinique, d'établir et de maintenir des relations avec d'autres centres de recherche en Suisse et à l'échelle internationale, et de sensibiliser le public aux réalisations des membres de ZNZ. Le directeur général travaille en étroite collaboration avec le comité directeur de ZNZ, qui est responsable de la stratégie globale du centre. Contexte du projet Le paysage de la recherche en neurosciences au sein du réseau ZNZ est diversifié. Des chercheurs issus de milieux tels que la biologie, la médecine, la psychologie, la biochimie, la physique, l'ingénierie, l'informatique et l'économie étudient des questions fondamentales sur le fonctionnement du cerveau dans la santé et les maladies. Cela stimule le développement de nouvelles technologies de diagnostic, de thérapie et d'intelligence. Au cours des dernières années, les membres de ZNZ ont contribué de façon significative aux progrès des thérapies pour la démence, la sclérose en plaques et les lésions de la moelle épinière, ainsi qu'aux technologies de neuroréadaptation, à l'imagerie cérébrale de pointe, aux applications ultrasoniques ciblées, à la recherche sur le sommeil, à la neuroéconomie et aux réseaux neuronaux artificiels. Student Research Assistant – Unity Frontend Development for Digital Einstein 10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Digital Character AI team at ETH Zurich's Computer Graphics Laboratory is looking for a Student Research Assistant to support the frontend development of our interactive AI avatar platforms. Our work focuses on lifelike digital humans powered by large language models, affective computing, and real-time rendering — deployed at high-profile events such as the World Economic Forum, Berlin Science Week, and GITEX. You can learn more about the Digital Einstein project here . Project background Digital Einstein is an award-winning AI avatar platform that brings Albert Einstein to life as an interactive conversational agent. Built on a Unity-based frontend integrated with speech recognition and real-time facial and body animations, it has been showcased at major international events. The backend is implemented in Python and orchestrates large language models for dialogue management and response generation. We are currently extending the platform to a new Digital Curie installation. As our team scales up, we are looking for a student assistant to primarily help maintain and further develop the Unity frontend for both avatars — with the option to also contribute to the Python/LLM backend. Job description
• Frontend maintenance and feature development in Unity for the Digital Einstein and Digital Curie avatar platforms
• Integration and testing of UI components, interaction flows, and real-time rendering elements
• Optionally: support on the Python/LLM backend (dialogue systems, model integration)
• On-site support at events and demonstrations (setup, visitor interaction, troubleshooting)
• Weekly team meetings (1–2 hours) to discuss progress and plan next steps
• Workload: 15 hours/week during semester, up to 41 hours/week during semester breaks (flexible) Profile
• Enrolled student at ETH Zurich or another Swiss university
• Strong hands-on experience with Unity (required)
• Interest in interactive systems or AI-driven applications
• Reliable, proactive, and comfortable working independently as well as in a team
• Willingness to provide on-site event support on occasion, including on weekends
• Knowledge of Python and/or large language models is a plus
• German language skills are a plus Workplace Workplace We offer
• Hands-on experience with a high-profile AI avatar platform showcased at international events (World Economic Forum, GITEX, and others)

• Collaborative, international team at ETH Zurich's Computer Graphics Laboratory

La posizione è ospitata dal gruppo Crop Science; un gruppo di lavoro vibrante e interdisciplinare nell'Istituto di Scienze Agrarie presso il Dipartimento di Scienze Ambientali dell'ETH di Zurigo. La ricerca fenotipante del nostro gruppo si concentra sullo sviluppo di metodi e modelli per determinare i tratti di rilevanza per l'allevamento di colture e test di varietà. Il gruppo di ricerca Agroscope Extension Arable Crops (Competence Division Plants and Plant Products) sviluppa soluzioni ecologiche per il controllo delle malattie, dei parassiti e delle infestanti e valuta le varietà vegetali per la loro idoneità in condizioni svizzere. Ci vuole un approccio olistico per creare sistemi agricoli sostenibili, convenienti e affidabili dal clima. Il progetto PhenoMix è un progetto congiunto di quattro gruppi di ricerca all'ETH di Zurigo, al Centro svizzero per la scienza dei dati e all'agroscopio. L'obiettivo generale di PhenoMix è quello di testare l'ipotesi che l'attuale tecnologia di fenotipazione del campo ad alto rendimento in combinazione con le valutazioni dei servizi fisiologici dell'impianto e dell'ecosistema può fornire una svolta per determinare genotipi che possono essere combinati con successo in miscele legume-cere agroecologicamente vantaggiose. Diverse varietà di legumi (peci, lenticchie) e cereali (wheat, avena, orzo) saranno coltivate in stand puri e in miscele sul campo fenotyping piattaforma FIP del gruppo Crop Science, in un campo sperimentale confinante e nei campi del contadino. I pacchetti di lavoro PhenoMix affrontano fenotyping, ecofisiologia vegetale, scienza dei dati e prestazioni agronomic-economiche con quattro studenti di dottorato, due postdoc e diversi tecnici assegnati a tali pacchetti di lavoro. Lo studente medico agro-economico istituirà e monitorerà esperimenti sul campo in loco e on-farm indagando su diverse miscele lentili-cereali valutando vari servizi ecosistemici. PhD Position: Agro-Economic Analysis of Legume-Cereal Mixtures (PhenoMix project) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken This doctoral student position is part of the project “ PhenoMix: Multidimensional field phenotyping of crop mixtures ”, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation. The position is hosted by the Crop Science group; a vibrant and interdisciplinary working group in the Institute of Agricultural Sciences at the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich. Our group’s phenotyping research focuses on the development of methods and models to determine traits of relevance for crop breeding and variety testing. The Agroscope research group Extension Arable Crops (Competence division Plants and Plant Products) develops ecological solutions for disease, pest and weed control and evaluates crop varieties for their suitability under Swiss conditions. It takes a holistic approach to create sustainable, cost-efficient, and climate-resilient arable farming systems. Project background PhenoMix is a joint project of four research groups at ETH Zurich, the Swiss Data Science Center and Agroscope. The overall objective of PhenoMix is to test the hypothesis that current high throughput field phenotyping technology in combination with plant physiological and ecosystem service assessments can provide a breakthrough to determine genotypes that can be successfully combined in agroecologically beneficial legume-cereal mixtures. Different varieties of legumes (peas, lentils) and cereals (wheat, oats, barley) will be grown in pure stands and in mixtures on the field phenotyping platform FIP of the Crop Science group, on a neighbouring experimental field and on farmer’s fields. The PhenoMix Work Packages address phenotyping, plant ecophysiology, data science, and agronomic-economic performance with four doctoral students, two postdocs and several technicians assigned to those work packages. The Agro-Economic doctoral student will establish and monitor on-site and on-farm field experiments investigating several lentil-cereal mixtures by assessing various ecosystem services. Job description This doctoral project will form an important cornerstone in the mosaic of the entire project with specific tasks and in alignment with the other PhenoMix doctoral students and postdocs for which recruiting is also going on currently. Overall tasks of the project include:
• Planning, conducting and evaluating field and post-harvest laboratory experiments
• Performing statistical analyses, including AI-based approaches
• Presentation of results at national and international events and publication in peer-reviewed and in practice-oriented journals
• Organisation of national workshops for growers, food industry and consumers
• Assistance in plot establishment, maintenance, monitoring, and harvest across all Work Packages of PhenoMi x. This full-time position is funded for four years. Salary and social benefits are provided according to ETH Zurich rules. The place of work will be at Agroscope in 8046 Zurich-Affoltern. Profile
• A MSc degree in agricultural sciences, biology, ecology or in a related field.
• Strong interest in applied interdisciplinary research and enjoyment of complex field experiments
• Experience in planning laboratory and field experiments as well as in statistical analyses (e.g. R)
• Performance-oriented, team player and open-minded personality
• Excellent standard of written and spoken English
• Good writing skills
• Driver’s license
• Experience in niche crops and good oral communication skills in German are beneficial Workplace Workplace We offer

Ce poste est accueilli par le groupe Crop Science, un groupe de travail dynamique et interdisciplinaire de l'Institut des sciences agricoles du Département des sciences des systèmes environnementaux à l'ETH Zurich. Notre recherche de phénotypage de groupe se concentre sur l'élaboration de méthodes et de modèles pour déterminer les caractéristiques pertinentes pour la sélection des cultures et l'analyse des variétés. Le groupe de recherche Agroscope Extension Arable Crops (Division de la concurrence Plantes et produits végétaux) développe des solutions écologiques pour lutter contre les maladies, les ravageurs et les mauvaises herbes et évalue les variétés de cultures pour leur adéquation dans des conditions suisses. chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Ricercatore Postdoctoral a Construction Heritage and Preservation 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo determinato Drucken La cattedra di Construction Heritage and Preservation è attualmente alla ricerca di un ricercatore post-dottorato a partire dal settembre 2026 o su accordo. La cattedra di patrimonio edilizio e conservazione si occupa di sfide teoriche e pratiche di raccolta, valutazione e conservazione dei monumenti. È affiliato all'Istituto per la conservazione e la storia delle costruzioni (IDB) e all'Istituto per la tecnologia in architettura (ITA) . La conoscenza dei metodi di costruzione tradizionali, dei materiali, dei principi di progettazione architettonica e dei processi di costruzione è essenziale per una gestione professionale e responsabile degli edifici storici. Per quanto riguarda il futuro sviluppo del patrimonio edilizio sembra altrettanto importante considerare i processi più giovani e anche attuali. I nuovi materiali da costruzione, i metodi di costruzione e i “trends” influiscono sempre più sull’architettura e nel settore dell’edilizia è possibile riconoscere un’accelerazione dell’implementazione di nuove idee e tecnologie. Attualmente, vi è una mancanza di conoscenza circa l'invecchiamento e la riparabilità di tali nuove costruzioni e la ricerca sulle conseguenze a lungo termine per lo stock di edifici sembra insufficiente. La ricerca si concentra su diversi stock edilizi, sia più vecchi che più giovani (e anche molto giovani), domande del loro valore come monumenti e sfide relative alla loro conservazione. In questo contesto, i lavori di ingegneria strutturalmente eccezionali in Svizzera e gli esempi costruiti di processi e metodi di costruzione di nuova concezione sono di particolare interesse. Le attività didattiche includono corsi elettivi e seminari di base che permettono agli studenti di studiare e discutere le questioni attuali in dettaglio. Postdoctoral Researcher at Construction Heritage and Preservation 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Professorship of Construction Heritage and Preservation is currently searching for a postdoctoral researcher to start in September 2026 or upon agreement. Project background The Professorship of Construction Heritage and Preservation engages with theoretical and practical challenges of methodical collecting, assessing and preserving of monuments. It is affiliated with the Institute for Preservation and Construction History (IDB) as well as the Institute for Technology in Architecture (ITA) . Knowledge of traditional construction methods, materials, architectural design principles and building processes is essential for a professional and responsible handling of historic buildings. With regard to the future development of the building stock it seems equally important to consider younger and even current processes. New building materials, construction methods and “trends” are increasingly affecting architecture and an accelerated implementation of new ideas and technologies can be recognised in the building sector. Currently, there is a lack of knowledge about the aging and reparability of such new constructions and research on long-term consequences for the building stock seems inadequate. Research focusses on diverse building stocks, both older and younger (as well as very young), questions of their value as monuments and challenges concerning their conservation. Within this context, the structurally outstanding engineering works in Switzerland as well as the built examples of newly developed construction processes and methods are of special interest. Teaching activities include elective courses and core seminars which allow students to study and discuss current issues in-depth. The lecture concentrates on the theoretical and practical basics of preservation. Furthermore, the professorship offers the academic continuing education programs which comprehensively and methodologically combine high academic standards with practical relevance and impart specific professional skills. Job description As a postdoctoral researcher, your responsibilities will include:
• Formulating and writing proposals for research grant applications (SNF, Innosuisse, EU Horizon, etc.)
• Contributing to ongoing research projects, including scientific publication efforts
• Co-leading publication projects
• Supporting teaching activities within the professorship, including further education programmes (MAS/CAS)
• Supporting the supervision of doctoral researchers within the professorship, and
• Taking on short- and medium-term projects within the framework of the Competence Center for Preservation at IDB Profile
• You have a Master's degree and a PhD in architecture, civil engineering, art history or technology history, or related fields
• You have experience of applying for and successfully obtaining third-party funding for research projects
• Knowledge of Swiss and international architectural heritage and building cultures is an asset
• You can demonstrate excellent written and oral communication skills in German and English Workplace Workplace We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society
• An interdisciplinary and diverse team of researchers in the fields of architecture, preservation, art and architectural history, building research, innovative building technologies and sustainability.

Contexte du projet Le professeur de construction Patrimoine et préservation s'occupe des défis théoriques et pratiques de la collecte méthodique, de l'évaluation et de la préservation des monuments. Il est affilié à l'Institut de préservation et d'histoire de la construction (IDB) ainsi qu'à l'Institut de technologie en architecture (ITA). La connaissance des méthodes de construction traditionnelles, des matériaux, des principes de conception architecturale et des processus de construction est essentielle pour une gestion professionnelle et responsable des bâtiments historiques. En ce qui concerne l'évolution future du parc immobilier, il semble tout aussi important d'envisager des processus plus jeunes, voire actuels. Les nouveaux matériaux de construction, les méthodes de construction et les tendances affectent de plus en plus l'architecture et une mise en œuvre accélérée des nouvelles idées et technologies peut être reconnue dans le secteur du bâtiment. À l'heure actuelle, on manque de connaissances sur le vieillissement et la réparabilité de ces nouvelles constructions et la recherche sur les conséquences à long terme pour le parc de bâtiments semble insuffisante. La recherche met l'accent sur la diversité des stocks de bâtiments, âgés et plus jeunes (ainsi que très jeunes), les questions de leur valeur en tant que monuments et les défis liés à leur conservation. Dans ce contexte, les travaux structuraux remarquables en Suisse ainsi que les exemples construits de procédés et de méthodes de construction nouvellement développés présentent un intérêt particulier. Les activités d'enseignement comprennent des cours facultatifs et des séminaires de base qui permettent aux étudiants d'étudier et de discuter en profondeur des questions actuelles. La conférence se concentre sur les bases théoriques et pratiques de la préservation. De plus, la chaire offre des programmes de formation continue qui combinent de manière complète et méthodologique des normes universitaires élevées avec une pertinence pratique et donnent des compétences professionnelles spécifiques. Description du poste En tant que chercheur postdoctoral, vous assumerez les responsabilités suivantes :
• formuler et rédiger des propositions de subventions de recherche (SNF, Innosuisse, EU Horizon, etc.)

• codiriger des projets de publication
• soutenir des activités d'enseignement au sein de la chaire, y compris des programmes de formation continue (MAS/CAS)

• entreprendre des projets à court et moyen terme dans le cadre du Centre de compétences pour la préservation du profil de la BID
• vous avez une maîtrise et un doctorat en architecture, en génie civil, en histoire de l'art ou en histoire de la technologie, ou dans des domaines connexes

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD candidato per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori a media frequenza ad alta potenza 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Il Laboratorio per sistemi elettronici ad alta potenza (HPE) presso il Dipartimento di tecnologia dell'informazione e ingegneria elettrica di ETH Zurigo conduce la ricerca internazionale leader sui sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza, che sono necessari, per esempio, nei futuri sistemi di distribuzione di energia elettrica per i Un'altra ricerca si concentra sui modulatori a impulsi a stato solido per applicazioni mediche (trattamento tomografia computer/cancro) e sugli acceleratori (CERN). Per la progettazione e l'ottimizzazione dei vari sistemi elettronici di potenza, sviluppiamo modelli multi-fisici avanzati / gemelli digitali / prototipi virtuali a livello di componenti e sistemi. Per un nuovo progetto di ricerca su Solid-State-Transformers per i futuri data center, stiamo cercando un: PhD candidate (100%) per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori ad alta potenza a media frequenza Descrizione del lavoro Siamo alla ricerca di individui altamente motivati con un eccezionale background accademico che sono interessati a perseguire un dottorato nell'importante e multidisciplinare area di ricerca di modellazione e ottimizzazione di trasformatori ad alta potenza, a media frequenza (MFT). I trasformatori compatti e altamente efficienti che operano a frequenze kilohertz sono componenti chiave dei convertitori DC-DC ad alta potenza, che sono il componente principale dei trasformatori a stato solido (SST). Tali SST sono necessari, per esempio, in futuri data center AI, dove il consumo di energia per rack di computer aumenta a livelli di diverse centinaia di kilowatt o addirittura megawatt. Per trasferire l'energia in modo efficiente dalla rete a CPU/GPU, sono necessarie tensioni di sistema più elevate nei centri di dati / rack per computer, e sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza efficienti basati su SST sono essenziali per il controllo del flusso di potenza altamente dinamico. Per spingere i limiti di efficienza e densità di potenza di questi SST si svilupperà modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori, che descrivono non solo le perdite (HF) nell'avvolgimento e nel nucleo, ma anche la distribuzione di raffreddamento / temperatura nel trasformatore, risonanze nell'avvolgimento a causa di capacità parassitarie, e isolamento elettrico. Si lavorerà anche sull'ottimizzazione della geometria del nucleo e dell'avvolgimento, lo sviluppo di concetti di raffreddamento avanzati per gli avvolgimento e il core, e la progettazione di soluzioni per collegare efficacemente gli avvolgimento ad alta corrente. Utilizzando i modelli e i concetti sviluppati, si identificherà le barriere tecnologiche per la potenza trasferibile e l'efficienza dei MFT. I modelli sviluppati dovrebbero essere integrati in procedure di ottimizzazione per sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza in modo computazionalmente efficiente. Ciò è essenziale per ottenere efficienze di sistema eccezionali e densità di potenza, così come ottenere un vantaggio competitivo. I modelli fanno parte anche di un continuo e più ampio progetto di sviluppo del framework di modellazione presso HPE, offrendo l'opportunità di collaborare con altri candidati PhD su diversi aspetti di modellazione. Per verificare i nuovi concetti e modelli sviluppati, si progetta e costruisce prototipi MFT, compresi i sistemi di conversione, per operare i MFT in condizioni realistiche. Profilo

PhD candidate for developing multi-physics models of high-power medium frequency transformers 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component and system level. For a new research project on Solid-State-Transformers for future data centres, we are looking for a: PhD candidate (100%) for developing multi-physics models of high-power medium frequency transformers Job description We are looking for highly motivated individuals with an outstanding academic background who are interested in pursuing a PhD in the important and multidisciplinary research area of modelling and optimising high-power, medium-frequency transformers (MFTs). Compact, highly efficient transformers that operate at kilohertz frequencies are key components of high-power DC-DC converters, which are the core component of solid-state transformers (SSTs). Such SSTs are required, for example, in future AI data centres, where power consumption per computer rack increases to levels of several hundred kilowatts or even megawatts. To transfer energy efficiently from the grid to CPUs/GPUs, higher system voltages are required in data centres/computer racks, and efficient power electronics converter systems based on SSTs are essential for controlling the highly dynamic power flow. For pushing the efficiency and power density limits of these SSTs you will develop multi-physics models of transformers, which describe not only the (HF) losses in the winding and the core, but also the cooling/temperature distribution in the transformer, resonances in the winding due to parasitic capacitances, and electrical insulation. You will also work on optimising the core and winding geometry, developing advanced cooling concepts for the windings and core, and designing solutions for efficiently connecting the high-current windings. Using the models and concepts developed, you will then identify technological barriers to the transferable power and efficiency of MFTs. The developed models should be integrated into optimisation procedures for power electronic converter systems in a computationally efficient way. This is essential for achieving outstanding system efficiencies and power densities, as well as gaining a competitive edge. The models are also part of an ongoing, wider modelling framework development project at HPE, offering the opportunity to collaborate with other PhD candidates on different modelling aspects. For verifying the new concepts and developed models, you will design and build MFT prototypes, including converter systems, to operate the MFTs under realistic conditions. Profile
• You must have a diploma/M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering with excellent grades
• Fundamental knowledge of power electronic converter systems
• Good communication skills
• Fluency in English
• The willingness to fully commit yourself as part of an international team.
• In addition, you should be interested in the detailed modelling and design of magnetic components and the optimisation of power electronic systems. Workplace Workplace We offer

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD-Kandidat für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von Hochleistungs-Mittelfrequenztransformatoren 100%, Zürich, Festdruck Drucken Das Labor für High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) am Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering der ETH Zürich führt international führende Forschungen zu Stromelektronik-Konvertersystemen durch, die beispielsweise in zukünftigen Energieverteilungssystemen für die Integration erneuerbarer Energieträger oder Zugfahrzeuge benötigt werden. Ein weiterer Forschungsschwerpunkt sind Festkörper-Impulsmodulatoren für medizinische Anwendungen (Computertomographie/Krebsbehandlung) und Beschleuniger (CERN). Für die Gestaltung und Optimierung der verschiedenen leistungselektronischen Systeme entwickeln wir fortschrittliche multiphysikalische Modelle/digitale Zwillinge/virtueller Prototypen auf Bauteil- und Systemebene. Für ein neues Forschungsprojekt zu Solid-State-Transformern für zukünftige Rechenzentren suchen wir einen: PhD-Kandidat (100%) für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von Hochleistungs-Mittelfrequenztransformatoren Jobbeschreibung Wir suchen hoch motivierte Personen mit einem hervorragenden akademischen Hintergrund, die daran interessiert sind, einen Doktortitel im wichtigen und multidisziplinären Forschungsbereich der Modellierung und Optimierung von hochleistungsfähigen, mittelfrequenten Transformatoren (MFTs) zu verfolgen. Kompakte, hocheffiziente Transformatoren, die bei Kilohertz-Frequenzen arbeiten, sind Schlüsselkomponenten von Hochleistungs-DC-Wandlern, die Kernkomponente von Festkörpertransformatoren (SSTs). Solche SSTs sind beispielsweise in zukünftigen KI-Datenzentren erforderlich, wo der Stromverbrauch pro Computer-Rack auf mehrere hundert Kilowatt oder sogar Megawatt ansteigt. Um Energie effizient vom Netz auf CPUs/GPUs zu übertragen, sind höhere Systemspannungen in Rechenzentren/Computer-Racks erforderlich und effiziente Stromelektronik-Wandlersysteme auf Basis von SSTs sind für die Steuerung des hochdynamischen Leistungsflusses unerlässlich. Um die Effizienz- und Leistungsdichtegrenzen dieser SSTs zu schieben, entwickeln Sie mehrphysikalische Modelle von Transformatoren, die nicht nur die (HF) Verluste in der Wicklung und dem Kern beschreiben, sondern auch die Kühl-/Temperaturverteilung im Transformator, Resonanzen in der Wicklung durch parasitäre Kapazitäten und elektrische Isolation. Sie arbeiten auch daran, die Kern- und Wickelgeometrie zu optimieren, fortschrittliche Kühlkonzepte für Wicklungen und Kern zu entwickeln und Lösungen für eine effiziente Verbindung der Hochstromwicklungen zu entwickeln. Mit den entwickelten Modellen und Konzepten werden Sie dann technologische Barrieren für die übertragbare Leistung und Effizienz von MFTs identifizieren. Die entwickelten Modelle sollten rechnerisch effizient in Optimierungsverfahren für stromelektronische Wandlersysteme integriert werden. Dies ist wichtig, um hervorragende Systemeffizienzen und Leistungsdichten zu erzielen und einen Wettbewerbsvorteil zu gewinnen. Die Modelle sind auch Teil eines laufenden, breiteren Modellierungs-Rahmenentwicklungsprojekts bei HPE und bieten die Möglichkeit, mit anderen PhD-Kandidaten zu verschiedenen Modellierungsaspekten zusammenzuarbeiten. Um die neuen Konzepte und entwickelten Modelle zu überprüfen, entwerfen und bauen Sie MFT-Prototypen, einschließlich Konvertersysteme, um die MFTs unter realistischen Bedingungen zu betreiben. Profil

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Candidat au doctorat pour le développement de modèles multiphysiques de transformateurs haute puissance à moyenne fréquence 100%, Zurich, tirage à terme fixe Drucken Le Laboratoire de systèmes électroniques haute puissance (HPE) du Département de technologie de l'information et de génie électrique de l'ETH Zurich mène des recherches de pointe sur les systèmes de convertisseurs électroniques de puissance, qui sont nécessaires, par exemple, dans les futurs systèmes de distribution d'énergie pour l'intégration de sources d'énergie renouvelables ou dans les applications de traction/véhicules électriques. Un autre axe de recherche porte sur les modulateurs d'impulsions à l'état solide pour les applications médicales (tomographie par ordinateur/traitement du cancer) et les accélérateurs (CERN). Pour la conception et l'optimisation des différents systèmes électroniques de puissance, nous développons des modèles multi-physiques avancés, des jumeaux numériques et des prototypes virtuels au niveau des composants et du système. Pour un nouveau projet de recherche sur Solid-State-Transformers pour les futurs centres de données, nous sommes à la recherche d'un candidat au doctorat (100 %) pour développer des modèles multiphysiques de transformateurs à moyenne fréquence haute puissance. Nous recherchons des personnes hautement motivées ayant une formation universitaire exceptionnelle qui sont intéressées à poursuivre un doctorat dans le domaine important et multidisciplinaire de la recherche de modélisation et d'optimisation des transformateurs haute puissance et moyenne fréquence (MFT). Les transformateurs compacts et hautement efficaces qui fonctionnent à des fréquences kilohertz sont des composants clés des convertisseurs DC-DC de haute puissance, qui sont la composante centrale des transformateurs à l'état solide (SST). Ces SST sont nécessaires, par exemple, dans les futurs centres de données AI, où la consommation d'énergie par rack d'ordinateur augmente à des niveaux de plusieurs centaines de kilowatts, voire mégawatts. Pour transférer efficacement l'énergie du réseau vers les CPU/GPU, des tensions plus élevées sont nécessaires dans les centres de données/racks d'ordinateur, et des systèmes de convertisseur électronique de puissance efficaces basés sur les SST sont essentiels pour contrôler le flux de puissance très dynamique. Pour repousser les limites d'efficacité et de densité de puissance de ces SST, vous développerez des modèles multiphysiques de transformateurs, qui décrivent non seulement les pertes (HF) dans l'enroulement et le noyau, mais aussi la distribution de refroidissement/température dans le transformateur, les résonances dans l'enroulement dues aux capacités parasitaires, et l'isolation électrique. Vous travaillerez également sur l'optimisation de la géométrie du noyau et de l'enroulement, le développement de concepts de refroidissement avancés pour les enroulements et le noyau, et la conception de solutions pour raccorder efficacement les enroulements à haut courant. En utilisant les modèles et les concepts développés, vous identifierez ensuite les obstacles technologiques à la puissance transférable et à l'efficacité des MFT. Les modèles développés devraient être intégrés dans les procédures d'optimisation des systèmes de convertisseur électronique de puissance d'une manière efficace par calcul. C'est essentiel pour atteindre des gains d'efficacité et des densités de puissance remarquables et pour obtenir un avantage concurrentiel. Les modèles s'inscrivent également dans le cadre d'un projet d'élaboration d'un cadre de modélisation plus large et en cours à HPE, offrant la possibilité de collaborer avec d'autres candidats au doctorat sur différents aspects de la modélisation. Pour vérifier les nouveaux concepts et modèles développés, vous concevez et construisez des prototypes MFT, y compris des systèmes de conversion, pour utiliser les MFT dans des conditions réalistes. Profil

chevron left Overview chevron left Overview Scientific Assistant (m/w/d) 60%-100%, Zurich, limited print Print The professorship for construction heritage and preservation is looking for a scientific assistant:in (Junior) to support teaching and research activities from September 2026 or by agreement. The professorship for construction heritage and preservation of monuments focuses on the theoretical and practical challenges of inventory, assessment and preservation of monuments. It is part of the Institute of Monumental Care and Historical Building Research and the Institute of Technology in Architecture (ITA). Knowledge of traditional design, materials, architectural design principles and construction processes is essential for professional and responsible handling of historic buildings. However, with regard to the future development of the building stock, it is also important to take into account younger and even current processes. Newly developed building materials, construction techniques and "trends" have a massive impact on architecture and an accelerated implementation of new ideas and technologies in the construction sector can be seen. It lacks knowledge of aging and repairability of such constructions, as well as investigations of long-term consequences and effects on the overall stock. As part of various research projects, both older and younger (and very young) structures are examined in terms of their heritage and in terms of the challenges of their preservation. In particular, the constructively exemplary engineering structures of Switzerland as well as the built witnesses of newly developed construction processes and techniques are at the forefront. Current issues are discussed and deepened in various courses. The lecture focuses on the theoretical and practical foundations of preservation. Job description
• They actively support and engage in ongoing teaching and research projects at the professorship
• They are involved in the design, preparation and implementation of courses including lectures, seminars and elective subjects, in-depth work and, if necessary, design studios and master's work
• They actively accompany and work on events, publication projects and other communication activities, such as scientific symposia profile

Projekthintergrund Die Professur für Konstruktionserbe und Denkmalpflege widmet sich theoretischen und praktischen Herausforderungen der Inventarisierung, Würdigung und Erhaltung von Denkmälern. Sie ist dem Institut für Denkmalpflege und historische Bauforschung sowie dem Institut für Technologie in der Architektur (ITA) zugehörig. Für den professionellen und verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit historischen Gebäuden ist die Kenntnis traditioneller Konstruktionsweisen, Materialien, architektonischer Entwurfsprinzipien und Bauprozesse unerlässlich. Im Hinblick auf die zukünftige Entwicklung des Baubestands erscheint es jedoch ebenfalls wichtig, auch jüngere und sogar aktuelle Prozesse zu berücksichtigen. Neu entwickelte Baustoffe, Konstruktionstechniken und «Trends» wirken sich massgeblich auf die Architektur aus und es ist eine beschleunigte Umsetzung neuer Ideen und Technologien im Bausektor zu erkennen. Es mangelt an Wissen über Alterung und Reparaturfähigkeit solcher Konstruktionen sowie Untersuchungen der langfristigen Folgen und Auswirkungen auf den Gesamtbestand. Im Rahmen verschiedener Forschungsprojekte werden sowohl ältere als auch jüngere (und sehr junge) Baubestände hinsichtlich ihrer Denkmalwürdigkeit und in Bezug auf Herausforderungen ihrer Erhaltung untersucht. Dabei stehen insbesondere die konstruktiv beispielhaften Ingenieurbauwerke der Schweiz sowie die gebauten Zeugen neu entwickelter Bauprozesse und -techniken im Vordergrund. In der Lehre werden in verschiedenen Lehrveranstaltungen aktuelle Fragestellungen diskutiert und vertieft. Die Vorlesung widmet sich vor allem den theoretischen und praktischen Grundlagen der Denkmalpflege. Stellenbeschreibung

Postdoctoral Position in Climate Science 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We invite applications for a full-time Postdoc position in the Climate Physics group of Prof. Reto Knutti and Prof. Erich Fischer at the Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science at ETH Zurich with a focus on understanding and quantifying weather and climate extremes in a warming climate. Project background The Postdoc position will be an integral part of the newly established National Competence Centre in Research NCCR CLIM+ . NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland’s transformation towards a climate-resilient society and trains a new generation of experts with strong disciplinary and transdisciplinary expertise. This project offers the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts in atmospheric and climate science within the NCCR CLIM+ as well as ETH Zurich. Job description
• We are seeking physical climate scientists with research experience in studying weather and climate extremes using coupled global and Earth System Models, regional climate and convection-permitting models, or AI weather models or in using process-based or statistical analysis of model results and reanalyses
• The applicant is expected to contribute to NCCR CLIM+ and to take leadership in the research field, including the supervision of students
• The position is for two years initially and can be extended subject to performance and availability of funding
• The starting date is as soon as possible but can be negotiated Profile
• Applicants must have a PhD in physics, atmospheric and climate sciences, statistics or related subjects, ideally working knowledge of climate models, and experience with shell scripting, high performance computing, or advanced statistics and data analysis frameworks (python, R)
• Regardless of background, the successful applicants will have an interactive personality, motivation to work with cutting-edge numerical climate models and their output, the ability to carry out research in an interdisciplinary and international environment, and a strong desire to disseminate results in conference talks and journal articles
• Fluency in English (written and spoken) and strong communication skills, in particular experience in the publication of research results in peer-reviewed journals, is required Workplace Workplace We offer
• We offer a dynamic and inspiring research environment, excellent work conditions, supercomputing infrastructure, and a large degree of freedom for the successful candidates to bring in their own research ideas and experience
• The Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science at ETH Zurich is a world-leading institute in the field of research on global and regional climate change at one of the leading international universities for natural sciences and technology chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:
• CV
• Publication list and brief paragraphs highlighting three scientific achievements
• Motivation statement and research ideas
• Names and contact details of three professional references Please include a detailed statement of motivation, scientific achievements and research ideas that you would be keen to work on in the context of this position. Application deadline is 30 May 2026 , but review of applications will continue until the positions are filled

• La date de début est le plus tôt possible, mais peut être négociée Profil

• Quel que soit le contexte, les candidats retenus auront une personnalité interactive, la motivation de travailler avec des modèles numériques de pointe et leur production, la capacité de mener des recherches dans un environnement interdisciplinaire et international, et une forte volonté de diffuser les résultats dans des conférences et des articles de revues

Scientific Collaborator / Teaching Assistant 50%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We are looking for a Scientific Collaborator / Teaching Assistant to join our team at ETH Zürich from July 2026 or by agreement. As part of the team, you will contribute to teaching and course preparation, including giving inputs and tutorials, organizing lectures, facilitating discussions, and supporting the writing and editing of academic and teaching-related texts. Project background Studio Maria Conen The Chair of Architecture and Housing approaches architecture as an ecological, social, and material practice shaping forms of living together. It addresses climate adaptation, resource cycles, and housing as a relational system embedded within landscape, water, and infrastructure. The Chair develops architecture as a mediating discipline, where spatial, material, and environmental logics converge. Through design and research, housing is understood as an interconnected, multi-scalar construct that integrates regenerative design, circular processes, and the interplay between natural and built systems. A particular focus lies on water as a spatial and formative driver, alongside a continuous exploration of form as a means to address these questions. Through teaching, research, and collaboration, the Chair fosters experimental design practices grounded in observation, making, and critical reflection, aiming to produce a precise and strong design for contemporary habitation. Job description For our Bachelor’s and Master’s design studio, we are looking for a part-time Teaching Assistant (50%).
• Teaching days: Tuesday and Wednesday
• Additional 10% workload distributed throughout the week The role includes:
• Contributing to teaching and course preparation, including inputs, tutorials, lectures, and discussions
• Preparing and supporting seminar weeks and study trips, including organizational and content-related tasks
• Supporting the writing and editing of academic and teaching-related texts We are looking for candidates with a strong interest in:
• Reuse and circular thinking
• Biodiversity and ecology
• Landscape
• Architectural representation (drawings, photography, models)
• Housing Responsibilities
• Prepare and organise teaching materials for the design studio
• Support and guide students in developing their projects (concept, structure, detailing)
• Provide technical and architectural expertise
• Contribute to the writing, editing, and proofreading of academic, research, and teaching-related texts Profile
• Degree in Architecture with 2–3 years of professional experience
• Strong design and technical skills
• Interest in academic teaching and research
• High level of initiative, strong communication skills, and a collaborative yet independent working style
• Fluency in English and German
• Preferably pursuing or planning to establish an independent practice Workplace Workplace We offer

chevron left Overview chevron left Overview Employees:in special waste management (m/w/d) 60%-80%, Zurich, unlimited print Print The Department of Safety, Health and Environment (SGU) advises, supports and advises all organizational units and members of ETH Zurich in matters of safety and health at work as well as on environmental protection at work. We have an appropriate emergency organisation for the event. In everyday life as well as in the event, we work closely with authorities and external agents. SGU coordinates the adoption of special waste at ETH and is responsible for its compliant disposal. In order to fulfill these tasks professionally and efficiently, we are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic personality in the Work Safety, Health and Environment section. Ready to take responsibility for the compliant special waste management? As part of the "Environment Team" section of Work Safety, Health and Environment You carry out operational and administrative tasks and perform the role of a hazardous goods officer in the field of special waste management. You take liquid and solid chemical waste into the special waste disposal sites of ETH, classify and drink it. Furthermore, it is one of your tasks to register special waste via the "VeVa-Online" tool and to create accompanying notes for transport. It is self-evident to inform you actively about new technologies and materials (e.g. lithium-ion accumulators, nanomaterials) and the associated development and to discuss this in the team. In addition, you advise ETH members on the topics of special waste management and hazardous goods and guide them through the special waste disposal centres, both in German and in English. Your work is the basis for the legal and environmentally sound disposal of special waste at ETH.
• Professional consultancy of the customer in German and English (Niveau B2)
• Openness for innovations and further developments in the field of specialized care
• Active participation and introduction of own ideas We offer your profession with effect: Be part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive changes in society. Working at the Vice-Presidium for Infrastructure and Sustainability (VPIN) means actively shaping the future of ETH Zurich - an inspiring, international and innovative institution. Your commitment creates the best conditions for excellence in teaching, research, knowledge transfer and sustainability at ETH Zurich. In an open, inspiring atmosphere, trust, reliability and mutual respect form the foundation of our cooperation. We offer you not only safety, but also a wide range of possibilities for further development. We are waiting for you to work in an innovative and value-adding environment that you can help shape and which opens up new perspectives.
